Grepped watch()/detectIntent/compress( across packages/ and apps/ excluding packages/ai/src and dist — zero hits, so nothing outside the AI package ever starts or consumes intent detection. createAI (index.ts:59-77) only wraps instance.destroy; it never subscribes to 'intent:detected' or calls instance.start. Demo App.tsx imports GuideBrain as a type only (line 1) and calls just gf.ai.chat (244) and gf.ai.generate (255). apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md:8 does make the 'automatically surfacing the right tour at the right moment' claim.

findings.title: An invalid selector from the model aborts the whole tour, or throws uncaught via hotspot()
findings.impact: `validateSteps` accepts any string as `target` with no syntax check. Tracing where it lands: `TourEngine._resolveTarget` does `document.querySelector(step.target)` (packages/core/src/engine/tour.ts:287), which throws `SyntaxError` on an invalid selector. That call sits inside the `try` in `_renderCurrentStep` (tour.ts:225-273), so the exception is caught — but the handler runs `this.emit('tour:error', ...)` then `this._doEnd(false)` (tour.ts:271-272), tearing down the entire tour and emitting `tour:abandon`. So one malformed selector in one AI-generated step kills all remaining steps rather than skipping that step. The unguarded path is worse: `gf.hotspot(sel)` -> `HotspotManager.add` does `document.querySelector(target)` with no try/catch (packages/core/src/engine/hotspot.ts:81), so the SyntaxError escapes to the caller — and that is exactly the pattern apps/docs/guide/ai-chat.md:81-84 tells users to write with model-produced highlight strings (`highlights.forEach(selector => gf.hotspot(selector, {...}))`). `ConversationalPanel.tsx:78` has the same `document.querySelector(sel)` on model output; it is inside the handler's try, so the user sees the answer message followed by "Something went wrong. Please try again."
findings.fix: Validate selectors at the trust boundary: in validation.ts, guard `step.target` with a `isValidSelector(s)` helper (`try { document.querySelector(s); return true } catch { return false }`, short-circuited to `true` when `!isBrowser()`), and do the same for `highlights` in `validateGuidedAnswer` (validation.ts:107-115). Independently harden core: wrap `_resolveTarget`'s `querySelector` in its own try/catch that returns `null` so a bad selector degrades to a centered/floating step instead of ending the tour, and wrap `HotspotManager.add`'s `querySelector` so it warns and returns `''` like the not-found path already does.
findings.verifierNote: validation.ts:35-37 verbatim — any string is accepted as target with no syntax check. Traced every hop: tour.ts:287 `return document.querySelector(step.target)` sits inside the try opened at line 225, and the catch at 267-273 does `this.emit('tour:error', ...)` then `this._doEnd(false)`; _doEnd(false) at 292-318 emits 'tour:abandon' (line 310) and nulls _machine/_flow, so remaining steps are gone rather than skipped. hotspot.ts:81 `const el = typeof target === 'string' ? document.querySelector(target) : target` has no try/catch — a SyntaxError escapes to the caller, which is exactly the loop at apps/docs/guide/ai-chat.md:81-85. ConversationalPanel.tsx:78 `document.querySelector(sel)` is inside the handler try whose catch renders 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'

findings.title: All three real providers JSON.parse() unconstrained model prose and silently swallow every failure
findings.impact: The only defence against non-JSON output is the system prompt string `Always respond with valid JSON only — no prose, no markdown fences.` No provider sets OpenAI's `response_format`, Anthropic's `output_config.format`, or Ollama's `format: 'json'`, and no provider strips markdown code fences. LLMs routinely wrap JSON in ```json fences or prepend a sentence; `JSON.parse('```json\n[...]```')` throws, the bare `catch` returns `[]`, and `gf.ai.generate('Walk me through checkout')` resolves with an empty array. The caller then does `gf.start({ steps: [] })` and sees a tour that renders nothing, with no error event, no log line, and no way to distinguish "model refused" from "model returned fences" from "API key wrong". The same swallow exists at anthropic.ts:62-67, ollama.ts:62-67, and for all three `detectIntent`/`answerQuestion` paths, where the fallbacks are the equally silent `{ type: 'exploring', confidence: 0 }` and `'Sorry, I could not answer that.'`.
findings.fix: Set structured output on each provider: `response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: {...} }` (or at minimum `{ type: 'json_object' }`) in openai.ts:55-63; `output_config: { format: { type: 'json_schema', schema } }` in anthropic.ts:45-50; `format: 'json'` in the Ollama request body at ollama.ts:36-47. Add a shared `stripCodeFences(text)` helper applied before `JSON.parse` as a belt-and-braces fallback. Replace every bare `catch {}` with a catch that emits a diagnostic (rethrow a typed `AIParseError`, or log the raw text under `debug`) so an empty result is distinguishable from a parse failure.
findings.verifierNote: openai.ts:74-79 matches the quoted block verbatim; identical swallow at anthropic.ts:62-67 and ollama.ts:62-67, plus the `{ type: 'exploring', confidence: 0 }` and 'Sorry, I could not answer that.' fallbacks in all three detectIntent/answerQuestion paths. No `response_format`, no `output_config`, no `format: 'json'` anywhere in packages/ai/src — the only defence really is the SYSTEM_PROMPT string at openai.ts:26-29 / anthropic.ts:18-21. No fence-stripping. Confirmed the caller sees nothing: brain.generate() emits 'steps:generated' with the empty array (brain.ts:106-108) rather than an error.

findings.title: watch() fires an uncapped LLM call on every 2-second user pause with no cooldown, batching or dedup
findings.impact: `push()` calls `scheduleDetect()` on every click, input, keydown, and scroll event (brain.ts:143, listeners at 159-162). Each 2s (default `intentDebounceMs`) lull therefore issues one full `provider.detectIntent()` round trip. There is no minimum-event threshold (a single stray scroll triggers a call), no cooldown between calls, no batching, and no dedup — and because the buffer is never trimmed after a detect, consecutive calls re-send largely identical `events.slice(-20)` payloads and are billed again each time. An ordinary user alternating short interactions and pauses produces on the order of 10-30 calls/minute/tab, i.e. up to ~1,800/hour for one open tab; a page left open with any periodic scroll activity bills indefinitely. Multiply by concurrent users and this is unbounded spend triggered by passive browsing, with no `maxCallsPerMinute`, no budget option, and no caching anywhere in the package. apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md:84 documents `{ autoWatch: true }` as a one-line way to switch this on, and `createAI(..., { autoWatch: true })` appears in apps/docs/api/ai/create-ai.md:45.
findings.fix: Add to `GuideBrainOptions`: a `minEventsBeforeDetect` threshold (skip the call when fewer than N new events accumulated), a `detectCooldownMs` floor between calls, and a `maxDetectsPerSession`/`maxDetectsPerMinute` cap. Track a high-water mark of already-analyzed events and skip the call when the buffer has not meaningfully changed. Trim or mark the buffer after each successful `detectIntent`. Document the per-user call rate and expected cost prominently in apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md next to the `autoWatch` example, and default `autoWatch` guidance to off.
findings.verifierNote: brain.ts:176-182 verbatim. push() calls scheduleDetect() unconditionally (line 143) and is wired to click/input/scroll/keydown at 159-162, with intentDebounceMs defaulting to 2000 (line 56). detectIntent (184-195) never trims eventBuffer — clearBuffer() exists at 264-266 but is called nowhere — so each call re-sends an overlapping events.slice(-20) (openai.ts:85). Grep for AbortController/timeout/retry/cache/maxCalls across packages/ai/src returns zero hits, so there is genuinely no cooldown, batching, dedup, or budget option. autoWatch is documented as a one-liner at apps/docs/guide/ai-intent.md:84 and used at api/ai/create-ai.md:45. The 10-30 calls/min figure is an estimate but the 2s debounce caps it at 30/min/tab, so the order of magnitude holds.

findings.title: With default variant weights, two different experiments assign every user identically (or identically inverted)
findings.evidence:
const hash = djb2(`${this.userId}:${experiment.id}`);
    const bucket = hash % totalWeight;
findings.impact: When `weight` is omitted (the default per line 13, and what src/index.ts:36-40, apps/docs/api/analytics/experiment-engine.md:31-38 and src/__tests__/experiments.test.ts:6-12 all use), two variants give `totalWeight === 2`, so the bucket is `hash % 2` — the low bit of djb2. Because `hash = h*33 ^ charCode`, the low bit reduces to `1 XOR (parity of the low bits of all characters)`, so the bit depends only on the parity of odd-valued characters in `userId:experimentId`. Verified empirically over 10,000 UUID-shaped user ids: `exp-one` vs `exp-two` agree on 100.0% of users; `tour-theme-2024` vs `cta-experiment` agree on 0.0% (perfectly inverted). The "Multiple Experiments" pattern documented at apps/docs/guide/ab-testing.md:61-81 is therefore fully confounded — every user in treatment of experiment A is in treatment of experiment B, so neither result is attributable. Three default-weight variants also mis-split: measured 33.4/33.7/32.9 for UUIDs and 31.0/32.4/36.6 for `u<i>` ids instead of 33.3 each.
findings.fix: Replace djb2 with a well-distributed 32-bit hash (murmur3 or FNV-1a with a final avalanche/mix step) and bucket over a fixed large space rather than `totalWeight`: `const b = hash(userId + ':' + experiment.id) / 0xFFFFFFFF` then walk normalised cumulative weights. Salt each experiment into the mix rather than relying on string concatenation for decorrelation, and add a test asserting cross-experiment agreement stays within a few points of 50% for default weights.

Default-weight usage is real (src/index.ts:36-40, api/analytics/experiment-engine.md:31-36, __tests__/experiments.test.ts:6-12). findings.title: Full URL and referrer are exfiltrated on every event with no scrubbing, sampling, or opt-out
findings.evidence:
url: typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.location.href : undefined,
    referrer: typeof document !== 'undefined' ? document.referrer : undefined,
findings.impact: `window.location.href` includes the query string and fragment. Real applications routinely carry `?email=`, `?token=`, `?reset_key=`, `?invite=`, `?session=`, SAML relay state, and Stripe/PayPal return parameters in URLs, and single-page apps put record identifiers in the path. Every one of these is forwarded verbatim to PostHog/Mixpanel/Amplitude/Segment and any webhook, on every one of the six tracked events, with no allowlist, no `sanitizeUrl` hook, and no way to disable — `CollectorOptions` (lines 22-27) has only `userId` and `globalProperties`. `document.referrer` leaks the previous page including its query string. A grep of packages/analytics for `consent|doNotTrack|optOut|sample|scrub|redact|anonym|gdpr|pii` returns zero matches, and the same grep across apps/docs returns zero matches, so nothing in the product or its documentation acknowledges this. For an EU deployment this makes the library a GDPR liability out of the box: no consent gate, no `navigator.doNotTrack` check, no opt-out switch, no deletion hook, and no documented event schema for a DPA.

Add `enabled`/`setEnabled()` and an `optOut()` that persists, honour `navigator.doNotTrack === '1'` unless explicitly overridden, add a `consent?: () => boolean` gate checked inside `send()`, and add `sampleRate`. Publish the resulting event/property schema in apps/docs and state exactly what leaves the browser.

CollectorOptions at :22-27 has only userId and globalProperties — no sanitizer, allowlist or disable flag. findings.title: All step-level events ship `flow_id: undefined`, making funnel and drop-off analysis impossible
findings.impact: `base(undefined, ...)` hardcodes `flow_id: undefined` for `step.viewed`, `step.exited` and `step.skipped` (lines 74, 79, 82). A product with three tours running produces an undifferentiated stream of step events with no flow attribution, so you cannot build a per-flow funnel, compute step-level completion, or measure where users drop off — the headline claim in apps/docs/guide/index.md:17. Worse, `properties` is spread last in `send()` (line 109), so a consumer who works around this by putting `flow_id` in `globalProperties` has it overwritten with `undefined` on every step event. `stepIndex`, present in the core payload for `step:enter`/`step:exit`/`tour:abandon`, is also dropped, so the ordinal position of a drop-off is unrecoverable.

Forward `payload.stepIndex` as `step_index` and `payload.stepIndex` on abandon as `abandoned_at_index`. Add a collector test asserting `flow_id` and `step_index` are set on `guideflow.step.viewed`.

The core payloads for step:enter/step:exit do carry stepIndex (core/src/types/index.ts:209-210) and it is dropped. findings.title: WebhookTransport docstring promises a navigator.sendBeacon unload fallback that is not implemented anywhere
findings.evidence: * Falls back to `navigator.sendBeacon` on page unload when the queue > 0.
findings.impact: `grep -rn sendBeacon packages/` returns exactly one hit: this comment. The actual unload path is `this._beforeUnloadHandler = () => void this.flush();` (line 46), an un-awaited async `fetch` with no `keepalive: true` and no `AbortSignal`. Browsers cancel in-flight non-keepalive fetches when the document unloads, so the entire queued batch is destroyed on every page navigation — precisely the case the docstring claims is handled. With the default `batchIntervalMs: 0` a single event still races unload; with `batchIntervalMs: 5000` (the value in apps/docs/guide/analytics.md:20) up to 5 seconds of tour events are lost per navigation, systematically under-counting `tour.completed` for users who complete a tour and immediately navigate.
findings.fix: Implement the documented behaviour: in the unload handler, `navigator.sendBeacon(url, new Blob([JSON.stringify(batch)], {type:'application/json'}))` and clear the queue on a `true` return, falling back to `fetch(url, {..., keepalive: true})`. Listen on `pagehide` and `visibilitychange`→`hidden` instead of `beforeunload` (which is unreliable on mobile Safari and disqualifies the page from the back/forward cache). Note that `sendBeacon` cannot carry the `Authorization` header, so the apiKey path needs a query-free alternative or the fetch+keepalive branch.
findings.verifierNote: webhook.ts:19 says exactly 'Falls back to `navigator.sendBeacon` on page unload when the queue > 0.' and grep across packages/ and apps/ returns only that comment plus its copy in dist/index.d.ts:133. The actual handler is webhook.ts:46 `this._beforeUnloadHandler = () => void this.flush();` and the fetch at :70 has no keepalive and no await, so unload does cancel it. Severity corrected: this is a docstring-vs-implementation gap causing unload data loss, serious but not exploitable/shipped-broken; also with the default batchIntervalMs:0 most events are already sent on track(), so only the trailing event races unload — the 5s-window loss requires the documented batchIntervalMs:5000.

findings.title: tour:error is not subscribed, so render failures are reported to analytics as user abandonment

findings.title: A hanging fetch permanently latches _flushing, silently disabling the transport and growing the queue without bound
findings.evidence: const response = await fetch(this.opts.url, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
findings.impact: There is no `AbortSignal`/timeout on the request. `flush()` guards with `if (this.queue.length === 0 || this._flushing) return;` (line 61) and only clears `_flushing` in `finally`. If the endpoint accepts the connection and never responds (hung load balancer, captive portal, proxy black-hole — the browser default is no timeout at all), `_flushing` stays `true` for the lifetime of the page. Every subsequent `track()` pushes to `this.queue` and every `flush()` returns immediately, so nothing is ever sent again, nothing is ever dropped, no warning is logged, and the queue grows unbounded for the whole session — `maxQueueSize` is only a flush *trigger* (line 53), never a cap. On a long-lived SPA with hotspots and hints this is a monotonic memory leak. `collector.flush()` also resolves instantly in this state, so `await collector.flush()` (README.md:336) returns success while nothing has been sent.
findings.fix: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(this.opts.requestTimeoutMs ?? 10000)` to `fetch` and add the option. Enforce `maxQueueSize` as a hard cap in `track()` — drop the oldest events (or newest, documented) and increment a `droppedCount` surfaced via a callback. Have `flush()` return the in-flight promise instead of `undefined` when `_flushing` is true so `await` actually waits.

findings.title: @guideflow/core declares "sideEffects": false while shipping CSS consumers must import — webpack will tree-shake the stylesheet away
findings.evidence: "sideEffects": false,
findings.impact: `"sideEffects": false` is a blanket assertion over every file in the package, including `dist/styles/*.css`. webpack 5 (and therefore Next.js, CRA, Rspack) uses it to elide imports whose bindings are unused — and a bare `import '@guideflow/core/styles'` has no bindings. The result is a production build where the tour renders completely unstyled while the dev build looks fine, which is the hardest class of bug for a user to diagnose. Every documented integration hits this: README.md:87, README.md:121, README.md:170, README.md:210, apps/storybook/.storybook/preview.ts:2, and the code the CLI scaffolds at packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:9.
findings.fix: Change packages/core/package.json:27 to `"sideEffects": ["**/*.css", "./dist/styles/*"]`. Leave the other five packages at `false` — none of them ship CSS.
findings.verifierNote: packages/core/package.json:27 is verbatim `"sideEffects": false,`. The package ships dist/styles/{index,tokens,themes,popover,dark,rtl,high-contrast}.css (I listed them) and every documented integration uses the bindingless `import '@guideflow/core/styles'` — README.md:87/121/170/210, apps/storybook/.storybook/preview.ts:2, packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:9 (CORE_TEMPLATE line 9). findings.title: release.yml publishes to npm after only a build — no lint, no type-check, no tests
findings.evidence:
- name: Build
        run: pnpm turbo run build --filter=!storybook --filter=!docs --filter=!e2e --filter=!@guideflow/demo

      - name: Create Release PR or Publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@v1
findings.impact: `release.yml` triggers on every push to master (line 5) and on `workflow_dispatch` (line 6), independently of ci.yml. tsup builds with esbuild, which strips types without checking them, so a package with failing `tsc --noEmit` or failing vitest suites builds successfully and is published to npm. Nothing in the job requires ci.yml to have passed — there is no `workflow_run` trigger and no `needs:`. A red CI run and a successful publish of the same commit can happen concurrently.
findings.fix: Insert `pnpm turbo run type-check ...`, `pnpm turbo run lint ...` and `pnpm turbo run test ...` steps between the Build and Create Release PR steps in .github/workflows/release.yml, mirroring ci.yml:37-44. Better still, gate the whole job on CI: `on: workflow_run: workflows: [CI], types: [completed], branches: [master]` plus `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`.
findings.verifierNote: .github/workflows/release.yml lines 37-42 match the quoted block verbatim, triggers are `push: branches: [master]` (line 5) and `workflow_dispatch` (line 6), and there is no `needs:`, no `workflow_run`, and no lint/type-check/test step anywhere in the job. The publish command (root package.json:17, `publish-packages`) is also build-then-`changeset publish` with no test gate. tsup/esbuild strips types without checking them, so a package failing `tsc --noEmit` or vitest still builds and publishes.

findings.title: package.json advertises a programmatic `exports` entry but tsup has dts:false, so consumers get no types
findings.impact: `packages/cli/tsup.config.ts:5` sets `dts: false`, and there is no `types`/`typings` field, so `import { PushOptions } from '@guideflow/cli'` resolves to an untyped module. `push.ts:8` exports `PushOptions` publicly, and the demo had to hand-duplicate it: `apps/demo/src/App.tsx:27` reads `/** Mirrors PushOptions from @guideflow/cli (which ships no .d.ts currently). */` followed by a copy of the interface — while apps/demo/src/App.tsx:834 tells readers it is "Typed by `PushOptions` from `@guideflow/cli`", which is false. Worse, the `"."` export actually resolves to the bin entry, which calls `program.parseAsync(process.argv)` at module scope (index.ts:50) — importing the package as a library executes the CLI.
findings.fix: Either drop the `exports` map entirely (it is a bin-only package) and keep `bin` only; or, if a programmatic API is intended, split `src/api.ts` from `src/index.ts` (bin), point `exports["."]` at the API entry with `types`, and set `dts: true` in tsup.config.ts:5.
findings.verifierNote: package.json:34-38 verbatim; tsup.config.ts:6 `dts: false`; no `types`/`typings` field anywhere in the manifest. `"."` and `bin.guideflow` both point at ./dist/index.js, and index.ts:50 calls `program.parseAsync(process.argv)` at module scope — so importing the package as a library does execute the CLI. push.ts:8 exports PushOptions, and apps/demo/src/App.tsx:26-31 hand-duplicates it under the comment '/** Mirrors PushOptions from @guideflow/cli (which ships no .d.ts currently). */' while App.tsx:834 tells the reader it is 'Typed by PushOptions from @guideflow/cli'. All quotes verified.

findings.title: @guideflow/cli has no tests and no test script — every command is unverified
findings.evidence:
"scripts": {
    "build": "tsup",
    "dev": "tsup --watch",
    "lint": "eslint src --max-warnings 0",
    "type-check": "tsc --noEmit",
    "clean": "rm -rf dist .turbo"
  },
findings.impact: There is no `test` script, no `__tests__` directory (core, react, ai and analytics all have `src/__tests__`), and `apps/e2e/tests` covers only browser tour behaviour (accessibility, spotlight-persistence, tour-flow). Root `pnpm test` -> `turbo run test` therefore skips the CLI entirely. Every defect in this report is the kind a single test would have caught: one assertion that `export foo.json` does not write to `foo.json`, one that `GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY` alone authenticates `push`, one that `init` twice does not clobber, one that `--framework vue` emits a Vue file. `type-check` and `lint` both pass clean (see packages/cli/.turbo/turbo-type-check.log), which is exactly why static gates gave no signal here.
findings.fix: Add `"test": "vitest run"` and `packages/cli/src/commands/__tests__/` with unit tests that import each `Command` and call `.parseAsync([...], {from:'user'})` against a temp dir (the commands are already exported as standalone `Command` objects, so this needs no refactor). Cover: export output-path derivation, export refusing to overwrite input, init idempotency, init non-TTY behaviour, push env-var auth against a stubbed `fetch`.
findings.verifierNote: packages/cli/package.json:44-50 verbatim — build/dev/lint/type-check/clean, no `test`. No __tests__ under packages/cli (find shows __tests__ only in packages/ai, analytics, core, react). Root package.json `"test": "turbo run test"`, so a package with no test script is skipped entirely. packages/cli/.turbo contains turbo-build.log, turbo-lint.log and turbo-type-check.log, consistent with the claim that the static gates pass while nothing exercises behaviour.

findings.title: apps/docs/api/cli.md documents an entirely fictional flag set for export and push

| `--flow <id>`     | —                    | ID of the flow to export |
| `--out <file>`    | `guideflow-export.json` | Output file path |
| `--config <file>` | `guideflow.config.ts` | Path to the GuideFlow config file |

Actual definitions: export.ts:19-21 = [file], -o/--output, --pretty; push.ts:23-26 = [file], -k/--api-key, -e/--endpoint, --env; push.ts:35 reads GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY. So every example at cli.md:86 and :108 fails as described. cli.md:32-33 claims `src/guideflow.ts` and `src/flows/welcome-tour.ts` while init.ts:95-96 writes `<outputDir>/guideflow.ts` and `<outputDir>/my-tour.ts` (auditor said lines 30-35 — the surrounding block; the claims are on 32-33). quick-start.md:88 does use `--api-key`, so the docs self-contradict. findings.title: `guideflow export foo.json` overwrites the user's input file in place, minified
findings.impact: `.json` is an accepted input extension (line 33), but the regex `/\.(ts|js)$/` does not match a path ending in `.json`. So for `guideflow export my-tour.json` with no `-o`, `outPath === src`. The file is read (line 34), `JSON.parse`d, and re-`JSON.stringify`d back over itself — and because `--pretty` defaults to `false` (line 21), the user's hand-formatted, version-controlled flow JSON is destructively minified to a single line with no backup, no confirmation, and a green `✓ Exported flow to my-tour.json` success message. There is also no `existsSync` guard on `outPath` in any branch, so an explicit `-o` silently clobbers whatever is there.
findings.fix: In export.ts:59 compute the default output as `src.replace(/\.(ts|js|json)$/, '') + '.flow.json'`, and add an explicit guard: if `resolve(outPath) === src`, error out. Add an `existsSync(outPath)` check that requires `--force` (or prompts) before overwriting any existing file.
findings.verifierNote: Lines 59-61 verbatim. `.json` is accepted at line 33, and /\.(ts|js)$/ cannot match a path ending in '.json' (it ends in 'on'), so outPath === src. `--pretty` defaults false (line 21). No existsSync guard on outPath in any branch (existsSync is used only on the input at line 25). Downgrading severity: the file is JSON.parse'd then JSON.stringify'd, so semantic content and key order survive — the loss is formatting/whitespace in a version-controlled file, not data destruction, and it is recoverable via git. A wrong-by-construction output path on an accepted input type is a serious defect, not shipped-broken-or-exploitable.

findings.title: `guideflow.config.ts` is documented in three places as the thing `init` creates, but no config file is ever written or read
findings.evidence: | `guideflow init` | Scaffold a `guideflow.config.ts` and example flow |
findings.impact: The same claim appears at packages/cli/README.md:24 and the file name is used as a documented default at apps/docs/api/cli.md:83 (`| `--config <file>` | `guideflow.config.ts` | Path to the GuideFlow config file |`). `init.ts:95-99` writes `guideflow.ts`, `my-tour.ts`, and `GuideFlowProvider.tsx` — never `guideflow.config.ts`. So there is no project-level configuration mechanism at all: `export`, `push` and `studio` cannot pick up a shared endpoint, api key, flow directory, or framework setting, and every invocation must re-specify everything on the command line. Repo-wide grep for `guideflow.config.ts` returns exactly three hits — README.md:533, packages/cli/README.md:24, apps/docs/api/cli.md:83 — all documentation, no producer and no reader. init.ts:95-99 writes guideflow.ts / my-tour.ts / GuideFlowProvider.tsx only. findings.title: `init` always prompts for the output directory, so it can never run non-interactively even with every flag supplied
findings.impact: The framework question has `when: !opts.framework` (line 78) but the outputDir question has no `when`, so it is always asked. `guideflow init --dir ./src --framework react` — a fully specified invocation — still blocks on a prompt. In a non-TTY context (CI, Docker build, `npx` inside a script, an agent harness) inquirer's input prompt has no stdin to read and the command hangs or throws, and there is no `--yes`/`--non-interactive` escape hatch anywhere in the package.

findings.verifierNote: init.ts:80-85 verbatim; the framework question carries `when: !opts.framework` (line 78) and the outputDir question carries no `when`, so inquirer.prompt is always entered. There is no --yes/--non-interactive option (only --dir and --framework at lines 66-67), so a fully-specified `guideflow init --dir ./src --framework react` still blocks. I did not execute it in a non-TTY, so 'hangs or throws' is the only unverified detail; either way it cannot complete unattended.

findings.title: `init` overwrites existing guideflow.ts / my-tour.ts / GuideFlowProvider.tsx with no check or prompt
findings.impact: `existsSync` is imported (line 1) and used for the directory (line 91) but never for the files. Re-running `guideflow init` — or running it in a directory that happens to contain a `guideflow.ts` — silently destroys the user's customised configuration and tour, then prints `✓ GuideFlow initialized!`. This is the documented workflow for "an existing project" (apps/docs/api/cli.md:24 "Scaffolds GuideFlow configuration files into an existing project"), so accidental re-runs are likely, and there is no dry-run flag to check first.
findings.fix: Guard each write: if the target exists, skip it and report `- skipped guideflow.ts (already exists)`, or prompt via the inquirer instance already imported. Add `--force` to opt into overwriting and `--dry-run` to preview. Track which files were actually written so the summary at lines 103-108 does not claim files it skipped.
findings.verifierNote: init.ts:95-100 verbatim. existsSync is imported at line 1 and used only at line 91 for the directory; the three writeFileSync calls have no existence check, no prompt, no --force/--dry-run, and line 102 prints `✓ GuideFlow initialized!` regardless. apps/docs/api/cli.md:24 does say 'Scaffolds GuideFlow configuration files into an existing project', so re-running against a populated directory is the documented use.

findings.title: `init --framework vue` / `svelte` silently scaffolds no framework code and reports success
findings.impact: The prompt at lines 74-79 offers `['react', 'vue', 'svelte', 'none']` and the `--framework` help at line 67 advertises `react | vue | svelte | none`, but only `REACT_TEMPLATE` exists in the file (there is no VUE_TEMPLATE or SVELTE_TEMPLATE). A Vue user selecting `vue` gets exactly the same two files as `none`, plus a success banner and `pnpm add @guideflow/core @guideflow/vue` (line 112) — with no wrapper, no plugin registration, and no hint that anything is missing. `packages/vue/src/plugin.ts` and `packages/svelte/src/index.ts` both exist, so the adapters are real; only the scaffolding is absent. `--framework` is also never validated: `guideflow init --framework angular` is accepted, skips the prompt (line 78 `when: !opts.framework`), and prints `pnpm add @guideflow/core @guideflow/angular` for a package that does not exist.

findings.title: `push` defaults to https://api.guideflow.dev/v1/flows — a service with no implementation, no signup path, and no documented key issuance
findings.evidence: .option('-e, --endpoint <url>', 'API endpoint', 'https://api.guideflow.dev/v1/flows')
findings.impact: The default endpoint is the only default a first-time user will hit. Nothing in the monorepo implements or deploys this API: a grep for `guideflow.dev` yields only this line, a marketing link in `packages/devtools/src/popup/popup.tsx:501`, a banner comment in `packages/core/tsup.config.ts:17`, and hardcoded copies in `apps/demo/src/App.tsx:178,783,843`. Document the expected POST contract (headers `Authorization: Bearer`, `X-GuideFlow-Env`; request body = FlowDefinition JSON; response `{id, url}`) so self-hosting is actually implementable, and mark Cloud as "planned" in README.md:536 and apps/docs/packages/cli.md:25 until it exists.
findings.verifierNote: push.ts:25 verbatim. Grep for `guideflow.dev` returns only that line, packages/devtools/src/popup/popup.tsx:501, packages/core/tsup.config.ts:17, apps/demo/src/App.tsx:178/783/843 — plus .claude/docs/MCP-AND-SKILLS.md:81 which itself states push ships pointed at 'a service that does not exist'. Grep for GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY across md/ts/tsx finds it only in push.ts:24/35/37 and that same .claude note — no doc anywhere explains how to obtain a key. push.ts:69 `await res.json()` is unconditional as claimed (though it sits inside the try, so a non-JSON 200 surfaces as the same 'Network error' message). README.md:536 'Publish flows to GuideFlow Cloud' verified.

findings.title: `--api-key` is a requiredOption, making the documented GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY env-var path unreachable dead code
findings.evidence: .requiredOption('-k, --api-key <key>', 'API key (or set GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY env var)')
findings.impact: Commander aborts with `error: required option '-k, --api-key <key>' not specified` and exit code 1 *before* the action handler runs. Therefore push.ts:35 `const apiKey: string = opts.apiKey || process.env['GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY'] || '';` can never see an empty `opts.apiKey`, and the guard at lines 36-39 (`Error: API key is required. Pass --api-key or set GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY.`) is unreachable. Concretely: `GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY=sk_live_x guideflow push my-tour.flow.json` fails outright, despite the option's own help text promising it works. This is the standard CI setup (secret in env, not on the command line), so the only usable path forces the key onto argv — where it lands in shell history and is visible to any process reading `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` or `ps`.
findings.fix: Change push.ts:24 to `.option('-k, --api-key <key>', 'API key (or set GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY env var)')` — Commander's `.env()` (v12: `.option(...).env('GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY')`) does this natively — and keep the runtime guard at lines 36-39 as the real enforcement point.
findings.verifierNote: push.ts:24 is verbatim `.requiredOption('-k, --api-key <key>', 'API key (or set GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY env var)')`. Commander runs _checkForMissingMandatoryOptions inside _parseCommand before the action handler and calls this.error(), so lines 35-39 (`opts.apiKey || process.env['GUIDEFLOW_API_KEY']` and the 'API key is required' guard) are unreachable dead code — the option's own help text advertises a path it forbids. The repo already knows this: .claude/agents/gf-docs-truth-checker.md:65 records the same contradiction. Downgrading from P0: the documented primary path (`--api-key`) works, so `push` is not shipped-broken outright; what is broken is the env-var/CI path plus the secret-on-argv consequence — a serious defect, not a total break.

findings.title: Attribute (Intro.js compat) tours render every step as a standalone 1-step tour with a "Done" button that ends the tour
findings.impact: Each scanned element becomes its own state holding exactly one step, so `machine.totalSteps === 1` for every step. DefaultRenderer then computes `isLast = index === total - 1` → `0 === 0` → true (default-renderer.ts:160), rendering the primary button as `i18n.t('done')` with `action: 'end'`, suppressing the Back button (`isFirst` also true), and omitting both the progress bar and the "Step X of Y" counter (`total > 1` guards, lines 168 and 183). Clicking the only primary button calls `instance.stop()` and abandons the tour instead of advancing; the sole way forward is the arrow keys. And because the last state carries `final: true`, that last step is never rendered at all (see final-state-steps-never-rendered). `autoInit()` — the entry point advertised in apps/docs/guide/migrate-intro.md:76 — produces exactly this shape.
findings.fix: Emit a single state containing all steps (`{ initial: 'tour', states: { tour: { steps, on: {} } } }`) so intra-state `nextStep()` drives navigation and totals/progress are correct; keep the multi-state form only if per-step transitions are needed. Alternatively make the renderer take flow-wide totals rather than per-state ones.
findings.verifierNote: intro-compat.ts:91-95 verbatim — one state per element, `steps: [step]`. So machine.totalSteps (machine.ts:61-63) is 1, and DefaultRenderer._buildHTML with index=0,total=1 gives isFirst=true and isLast=true (lines 159-160): the default actions array (162-165) drops the Back button and renders the primary as `i18n.t('done')` with `action: 'end'`; both the progress bar (line 168) and 'Step X of Y' (line 183) are gated on `total > 1`. 'end' maps to instance.stop() → _engineEnd() → _doEnd(false) (index.ts:184, tour.ts:159-161), i.e. abandon. Only the ArrowRight path reaches nextStep() → send('NEXT'). The last state carries `final: true`, so per the confirmed final-state bug its step never renders. autoInit (index.ts:382-387) calls scanAttributeTour directly; migrate-intro.md:76 advertises it.

findings.title: Cross-tab sync is wired only on the resume path, leaks an instance per start(), and applies snapshots from other flows
findings.impact: Three problems in four lines. (1) The constructor runs only inside `if (snapshot && !snapshot.completed)`, so a fresh start (no snapshot) or a start without `context.userId` never creates a channel — `_saveProgress`'s `_broadcastSync?.broadcast(...)` (index.ts:338) is a no-op and nothing is ever published. apps/docs/guide/persistence.md:76 claims "GuideFlow uses BroadcastChannel to sync tour state across browser tabs... This works out of the box with no configuration required." (2) Every resume-path `start()` overwrites `_broadcastSync` without calling `destroy()` on the previous one, leaking a live `BroadcastChannel` plus its listener per start; only the last one is destroyed by `destroy()`. (3) The handler never checks `snap.flowId === engine.flowId`, so a tab running flow B applies a snapshot broadcast for flow A whenever the two flows share a state name (`restore` only validates that the state exists in the *current* flow).

findings.title: Progress is never persisted for the first step or on abandon — only next/prev/goTo/send save
findings.impact: `_saveProgress()` is called only from the `next`/`prev`/`goTo`/`send` wrappers (index.ts:271, 276, 281, 286). findings.title: `content.html` "sanitiser" is regex-based and bypassable — unquoted javascript: URLs and unclosed iframes survive

findings.impact: `StepContent.html` is typed with the promise "Raw HTML — sanitised by renderer" (types/index.ts:36) and is injected via `el.innerHTML = this._buildHTML(...)` (default-renderer.ts:93), so authors will feed it CMS/AI/user content. The tag rules require a closing tag: ``) is not matched by `/<\s*iframe[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\s*\/\s*iframe\s*>/gi`, and `srcdoc` is not in the attribute allow-list, so it renders and executes. findings.title: showIf is evaluated forward-only, so prev() past a hidden step jumps forward again — Back becomes a no-op
findings.impact: The skip loop always advances with `nextStep()` regardless of how the step was reached. With steps [s1, s2(showIf:false), s3], pressing Back on s3 runs `prevStep()` → index 1 → the loop sees s2 hidden → `nextStep()` → index 2 → s3 renders again. The user cannot go back past a hidden step; the Back button appears dead and each press emits a spurious `step:skip` for s2 plus a `step:exit`/`step:enter` pair for s3. If s2 is the only step before s3 in that state, back navigation is impossible. Worse, when the hidden step is the last in a final-less state, the loop can walk forward and `_doEnd(true)` — pressing Back completes the tour.
findings.fix: Pass the traversal direction into `_renderCurrentStep(direction: 'forward' | 'backward' = 'forward')` and use `prevStep()` inside the skip loop when moving backward (ending the loop at index 0 by re-rendering the nearest visible step, or ending the tour only in the forward case).

With [s1, s2(showIf false), s3] at index 2, Back → index 1 → hidden → nextStep() → index 2 → s3 re-renders, emitting a spurious step:skip for s2 and a step:exit/step:enter pair for s3. One sub-claim does not hold: the 'pressing Back completes the tour' case is unreachable, since prevStep can only land on an index strictly below the current one and therefore never on the state's last step. findings.title: watchAttributeTour re-fires on GuideFlow's own DOM insertions, restarting the tour in a loop

findings.title: GF_FLOWS_LIST postMessages raw FlowDefinitions containing functions — silently swallowed on one path, uncaught throw on the other
findings.impact: `FlowDefinition.states[*]` carries `onEntry?: (context) => void` and `onExit?: (context) => void` (packages/core/src/types/index.ts:97-99); `Step.content` may be `() => MaybePromise<StepContent>`, `Step.showIf` is a function, `Step.target` may be an `HTMLElement`, and transitions may carry a `guard` function (types/index.ts:57-60, 76-78). None of these survive structured clone, so `postMessage` throws `DataCloneError` for any non-trivial flow. Here the catch swallows it and the Flows tab silently shows "No flows registered on this page" — a lie. On the other path, `case 'GF_LIST_FLOWS'` at bridge.ts:142-148 has no try/catch at all, so the popup's Refresh button and the panel's list-flows command throw an uncaught error into the host page's console. Either way the Flows tab is empty for exactly the flows worth inspecting.
findings.fix: Serialize flows through a sanitizer before posting: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(flows, (k, v) => typeof v === 'function' ? `[fn ${k}]` : v instanceof Element ? `[Element ${v.tagName}]` : v))`. Wrap the `GF_LIST_FLOWS` post in try/catch and post a `GF_FLOWS_ERROR` on failure so the panel can render a real error state instead of an empty list.
findings.verifierNote: bridge.ts:93-103 verbatim with the postMessage inside the try/catch; bridge.ts:142-149 (GF_LIST_FLOWS) has no try/catch. Verified that real in-repo flows carry functions: apps/demo/src/flows/onboarding.ts:131 has `guard: (ctx) => ...` and 134/181 have `onEntry: (ctx) => ...`, and core listFlows (packages/core/src/index.ts:304-306) returns the registered FlowDefinition objects verbatim. Structured clone therefore throws for the demo's own flows — silently on one path, uncaught on the other.

findings.title: runTour puts each step in its own state, so the popover always shows "1 of 1" and Back never works
findings.impact: Core computes `totalSteps` as `this.currentSteps.length` — the length of the *current state's* `steps` array (packages/core/src/fsm/machine.ts:61-63) — and passes it to `renderStep(step, content, index, total)` (engine/tour.ts:265). With one step per state, every step renders as "1 of 1" and any progress indicator is permanently full. Worse, `prev()` calls `this._machine.prevStep()`, which returns false at `stepIndex === 0` and has no cross-state fallback (machine.ts:101-108) — so the Back button in a DevTools-built tour re-renders the same step forever. Forward navigation works only because `nextStep()` falls back to `send('NEXT')` (machine.ts:96-97). Every tour the visual builder produces has a broken step counter and a broken Back button.
findings.fix: Emit a single state containing all steps: `{ id, initial: 'main', states: { main: { steps: steps.map(...), final: true } } }`. That gives correct `totalSteps`, working `prev()`, and a much smaller flow definition. Reserve multi-state output for when the builder actually supports branching.
findings.verifierNote: app.tsx:426-442 puts exactly one step in each `step-${i}` state. packages/core/src/fsm/machine.ts:61-63 defines `totalSteps` as `this.currentSteps.length` (state-scoped, line 50), passed to renderStep at engine/tour.ts:265 — so every step renders as 1 of 1. machine.ts:101-108 `prevStep()` returns false at stepIndex 0 with no cross-state fallback, while `nextStep()` (94-97) does fall back to `send('NEXT')`, exactly as claimed.

findings.title: The "Load" button on every saved tour is a no-op stub — the tour's steps are never loaded into the builder
findings.impact: The parameter is named `_tour` and is never read. Clicking Load switches to the Builder tab and clears the selected element — the saved tour's `steps` are discarded. `BuilderTab` holds `steps` in its own `useState` (app.tsx:340) with no setter prop, so there is no wiring by which a saved tour could ever be loaded. Combined with the fact that the panel's builder state is not persisted, Save is effectively write-only: you can save a tour and see it listed, but you can never get it back to edit it. The round trip advertised by the Flows tab is broken.
findings.fix: Lift `steps`/`flowName` out of `BuilderTab` into `App` (or pass `initialSteps`/`onLoad` props), and implement `onLoadSaved={(tour) => { setFlowName(tour.name); setSteps(tour.steps); setTab('builder'); }}`.
findings.verifierNote: app.tsx:1246-1253 verbatim — parameter is `_tour`, body only calls `setTab('builder')` and a timeout `setSelectedElement(null)`. BuilderTab owns `steps` in local `useState` (line 340) and its prop list (324-337) has no steps/setSteps, so no wiring exists. Save is therefore write-only.

findings.title: All per-tab state lives in service-worker module scope and is lost when MV3 suspends the worker; nothing re-detects
findings.impact: MV3 terminates an idle service worker after ~30s. `detectedTabs` is populated only by a `GF_DETECTED` message, which the bridge sends on page load or on an explicit `GF_PROBE`. After the worker restarts there is no re-hydration and nothing sends `GF_PROBE` (the popup never does). So: load a GuideFlow page, wait 30 seconds, click the toolbar icon → the popup reports "GuideFlow not detected", Events captured 0, no active tour, and the Pick Element / Record / Refresh buttons are all disabled. The badge and every popup feature are unusable in normal use.
findings.fix: Persist `detectedTabs`/`eventCounts`/`lastEvents`/`activeTours` to `chrome.storage.session` on write and lazily read on message handling, and have the popup send `GF_PROBE` to the content script on mount so detection is re-established rather than assumed lost.
findings.verifierNote: service-worker.ts:16-23 verbatim; all five maps/sets are module scope with no chrome.storage rehydration (the only storage use is GF_SAVE_FLOW/GF_LOAD_FLOWS at 173-192). `detectedTabs` is only added to on GF_DETECTED (line 109-112), which the bridge sends from `relay()` — reached on page load or on GF_PROBE. The popup (popup.tsx:259-287) sends only GF_GET_STATE, never GF_PROBE/GF_DEVTOOLS_OPEN on mount, and bridge.ts:195-206 stops retrying once `__guideflow` is found. So after worker suspension the popup reports not-detected and gates its buttons on it (popup.tsx:377,386,402).

findings.title: Recording started from the popup discards every captured step — the service worker only forwards them to an open DevTools port
findings.impact: The popup's Record button (`src/popup/popup.tsx:295-301`) sends `GF_START_RECORDING` and then calls `window.close()`. The content script captures clicks and emits `GF_RECORDED_STEP` messages, but the service worker has no handler that stores them — the only sink is `devtoolsPorts.get(tabId)`. With DevTools closed (the entire point of a popup-driven workflow), every recorded step is silently dropped. There is no buffer, no `chrome.storage` write, and no UI in the popup that could ever display recorded steps. A user records a ten-click flow, reopens the popup, and finds nothing — with no error.
findings.fix: Add a `recordedSteps` per-tab buffer in the service worker persisted to `chrome.storage.session` (survives popup close and SW suspend), append on `GF_RECORDED_STEP`, expose it via `GF_GET_STATE`, and render a recorded-steps list with Import/Export in popup.tsx. Alternatively disable the popup's Record button until a DevTools panel port exists, so the failure is at least visible.
findings.verifierNote: service-worker.ts:149-153 is the only sink for content-script messages and it is `devtoolsPorts.get(tabId)`. I grepped the package: no GF_RECORDED_STEP handler, no buffer, no chrome.storage write for recorded steps. popup.tsx:295-301 sends GF_START_RECORDING then `window.close()`, and popup.tsx has no recorded-steps UI at all. Claim is accurate. Downgrading to P1: it is a broken feature in one entry point (the DevTools-panel path does work), not a shipped break of the host page like the bridge P0.

findings.title: Popup "Run" hands the raw stored record to gf.start(), which expects a FlowDefinition
findings.impact: The stored value is what `GF_SAVE_FLOW` wrote: `{ id, name, steps: StepDraft[], savedAt }` (service-worker.ts:173-181 persisting the panel's payload from app.tsx:451). `gf.start()` is `async start(flow: FlowDefinition<TContext>, context?)` and immediately reads `flow.initial`/`flow.states`, both `undefined` here. The bridge wraps the call in try/catch and logs `[GuideFlow bridge] Failed to start tour:` to the page console (bridge.ts:136-138), so from the popup's perspective the ▶ button closes the popup and nothing happens — no error surfaces in the extension UI at all. Every saved tour is unrunnable from the popup.
findings.fix: Store the FlowDefinition (see export-json-wrong-shape) alongside the editable draft, and have the popup send the FlowDefinition. Also propagate the bridge's start failure back as a `GF_TOUR_START_FAILED` message so the popup/panel can show it instead of the page console.
findings.verifierNote: popup.tsx:303-310 verbatim. The stored value is what service-worker.ts:173-181 wrote from app.tsx:449-452 — `{id, name, steps: StepDraft[], savedAt}` with no `initial`/`states`. bridge.ts:132-139 wraps gf.start in try/catch that only console.errors into the page, so the popup surfaces nothing.

findings.title: buildSelector emits an unanchored 4-level :nth-child path that frequently matches the wrong element
findings.impact: The loop stops after 4 ancestors and never anchors the path at `html`, `body`, or `:scope`, so the result is a floating descendant pattern like `div:nth-child(2) > div:nth-child(1) > ul:nth-child(1) > li:nth-child(3)`. In any real app that repeats layout structure (nav + main, card grids, table rows, modal + page duplicating a shell), that pattern matches many nodes and `document.querySelector` picks the first — which is often not the element the user clicked. The function also never validates its own output: nothing calls `document.querySelectorAll(sel).length === 1`. Every downstream feature (Run, Preview 👁, exported step targets) then highlights or spotlights the wrong element with no warning. The comment on line 244 claims "for a unique selector", which is not what the code produces.
findings.fix: Walk to `document.body`/`document.documentElement` rather than stopping at 4 levels, prefix with `body > ` (or `:scope`), and add a verification loop: build progressively longer paths and return the first for which `document.querySelectorAll(candidate).length === 1`; if none is unique, return the full path and set an `ambiguous: true` flag on the `GF_ELEMENT_SELECTED` payload so the panel can warn.
findings.verifierNote: inspector.ts:243-256 verbatim; the loop caps at 4 parts and never prefixes html/body/:scope, and nothing in the file calls querySelectorAll to check uniqueness. Only for shallow elements does the walk terminate at `html` (parentElement null) and become anchored; for typical app DOM depth the result is a floating descendant pattern. The comment on 243 does claim uniqueness the code does not deliver.

"scripts": {

findings.title: ai-generate guide documents an options object as generate()'s second argument; it is a DOM root

findings.title: Docs claim cross-tab sync works automatically, but BroadcastSync is only created on a resumed tour
findings.evidence:
GuideFlow uses `BroadcastChannel` to sync tour state across browser tabs. When a user completes a step in one tab, all other tabs update automatically.

This works out of the box with no configuration required.
findings.impact: In packages/core/src/index.ts the only assignment to `_broadcastSync` is at line 254, inside `if (snapshot && !snapshot.completed)` — which itself sits inside `if (userId)`. So the channel is created only when a user has a *previously saved, incomplete* snapshot at start time. On a first-ever tour, or any tour without `context.userId`, `_broadcastSync` stays `null` and `_saveProgress`'s `_broadcastSync?.broadcast(...)` (line 338) is a no-op. Cross-tab sync therefore does not work "out of the box with no configuration" — it requires a userId *and* a second run. apps/docs/api/progress-store.md:55 repeats the claim ("works automatically when persistence is enabled") and README.md:26 advertises "cross-tab sync via BroadcastChannel" as a headline feature. No test covers the createGuideFlow wiring at all — there is no test file for packages/core/src/index.ts.
findings.fix: Create `BroadcastSync` unconditionally whenever `_config.context?.userId` is set (move it out of the snapshot branch in packages/core/src/index.ts), and tear it down in `destroy()`. Add packages/core/src/__tests__/create-guide-flow.test.ts covering: fresh start with userId creates the channel, dismissed flows are skipped, and an incomplete snapshot restores state and step index.
findings.verifierNote: persistence.md:74-78 is verbatim ('This works out of the box with no configuration required'). packages/core/src/index.ts has exactly one assignment to _broadcastSync, at line 254, nested inside `if (snapshot && !snapshot.completed)` (249) inside `if (userId)` (244). On a first run or without context.userId it stays null and `_broadcastSync?.broadcast(...)` at line 338 is a no-op. api/progress-store.md:55 repeats 'This works automatically when persistence is enabled' and README.md:26 advertises it as a headline feature. No test file exists for src/index.ts.

findings.title: GuideBrain API reference documents a stopWatch() method that does not exist and gets three signatures wrong
findings.evidence:
### `stopWatch()`

Stops monitoring user events and clears the internal event buffer.

```ts
stopWatch(): void
```
findings.impact: `GuideBrain` (packages/ai/src/brain.ts) has no `stopWatch` member at all — `gf.ai.stopWatch()` throws `TypeError: gf.ai.stopWatch is not a function`. Cleanup is done via the function returned by `watch()`, which the same page documents as `watch(): void` (line 61) — so a reader following this page has no working way to stop intent monitoring and leaks four document-level listeners. `compress(steps)` at line 83 is documented as single-argument, but brain.ts:211 is `compress(steps: Step[], instance: GuideFlowInstance, userId?: string)` with `instance` required. And lines 50-51 print `answer.answer` and `answer.stepId`, while `GuidedAnswer` (types/index.ts:286) is `{ text, highlights, confidence?, suggestedSteps? }` — both log `undefined`.
findings.fix: Delete the `stopWatch()` section; document `const stop = gf.ai.watch()` / `stop()`. Correct the signatures to `watch(): () => void` and `compress(steps: Step[], instance: GuideFlowInstance, userId?: string): Promise<Step[]>`. Replace `answer.answer`/`answer.stepId` with `answer.text`/`answer.highlights` here and at api/ai/create-ai.md:54 and guide/ai.md:77-78.

Doc lines 50-51 log `answer.answer`/`answer.stepId` while GuidedAnswer (types/index.ts:286) is {text, highlights, confidence?, suggestedSteps?}. findings.title: The i18n guide documents setLocale() and arbitrary translation keys; neither exists
findings.evidence: gf.i18n.setLocale('es')
findings.impact: `I18nRegistry` (packages/core/src/i18n/index.ts) exposes `register(locale, strings: Partial<Locale>)`, `use(locale)`, `t(key: keyof Locale, vars?)`, `activeLocale`, and `getLocale(locale?): Locale`. There is no `setLocale` — `gf.i18n.setLocale('es')` is a TypeError at runtime. Worse, `Locale` is a closed interface of exactly 8 UI strings (next, prev, close, skip, stepOf, done, openHint, closeHint), so the guide's entire premise — registering `'tour.welcome.title'` and calling `gf.i18n.t('tour.welcome.title')` — is impossible: `register` rejects the excess properties and `t` rejects the key. The documented API table at i18n.md:84-87 lists four methods of which three (`setLocale`, `getLocale()` returning a string, `t(key)` for arbitrary keys) do not match the implementation. The fallback description ("falls back to the default locale (first registered locale)") is also wrong — i18n/index.ts:46 falls back to the hard-coded `EN` constant.
findings.fix: Rewrite apps/docs/guide/i18n.md around the real API: `gf.i18n.register('es', { next: 'Siguiente', prev: 'Anterior', done: 'Hecho' })` then `gf.i18n.use('es')`, and state explicitly that only the 8 built-in chrome strings are translatable while step content must be localised by the caller (e.g. via an async `content` function). Update the README bullet "i18n — extensible translation registry" to match.
findings.verifierNote: i18n.md:39 is verbatim `gf.i18n.setLocale('es')`. i18n/index.ts exposes register/use/t/activeLocale/getLocale — no setLocale (verified by full read of the 64-line file). Locale is the closed 8-key interface at lines 6-15, so `register('en', {'tour.welcome.title': ...})` and `t('tour.welcome.title')` are both type errors and return the wrong thing. The fallback claim is also wrong: line 45 `this._locales.get(this._active) ?? EN` and line 46 `locale[key] ?? EN[key]` fall back to the hard-coded EN constant, not the first registered locale.

findings.title: Intent-detection docs describe an IntentSignal shape and field the code does not produce
findings.impact: The real `IntentSignal` (packages/core/src/types/index.ts:279) is `{ type; element?: string; confidence: number; duration?: number }` — there is no `context` object, so `signal.context.page` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. `validateIntentSignal` (packages/ai/src/validation.ts) never constructs a `context` field either. Separately, apps/docs/guide/ai.md:54 branches on `signal.intent === 'checkout'` — `intent` is not a field on the returned object (it is only accepted as an *input* alias by the validator) and `'checkout'` is not one of the four legal `type` values, so that documented handler can never fire.
findings.fix: Replace the fabricated interface in ai-intent.md with the actual `IntentSignal` from packages/core/src/types/index.ts:279, and fix guide/ai.md:54 to `if (signal.type === 'confused' && signal.confidence > 0.8)`.

Real IntentSignal (types/index.ts:279) is `{type; element?; confidence; duration?}` — no `context`. ai.md:54 branches on `signal.intent === 'checkout'`; `intent` is not a field on IntentSignal and 'checkout' is not one of the four legal type values, so that handler can never fire.

findings.title: Both migration guides map old APIs onto GuideFlow events and options that do not exist
findings.evidence:
| `onDestroyStarted` | `gf.on('tour:end', handler)` |
| `allowClose` | `step.allowDismiss` |
| `stagePadding` | `config.spotlight.padding` |
findings.impact: `TourEvents` (packages/core/src/types/index.ts:202-216) contains no `tour:end` — the real events are `tour:complete` and `tour:abandon`. `Step` (types/index.ts:53-72) has no `allowDismiss`. migrate-driver.md:55 shows `createGuideFlow({ spotlight: { opacity: 0.75 } })` but `SpotlightOptions` (types/index.ts:121-133) declares `overlayOpacity`, not `opacity`, so it is a TS excess-property error and a silent no-op. migrate-intro.md is equally wrong: line 15 maps `.exit()` to `gf.end()` (the `GuideFlowInstance` interface exposes `stop()`, not `end()`), and lines 19-20 map `.oncomplete`/`.onexit` to `tour:end` and `tour:skip`, neither of which exists. Because `on()` is typed against `TourEvents`, all of these are compile errors *and* handlers that can never fire — so a migrating user's completion tracking silently breaks. README.md:540-554 compounds this by claiming `data-intro`/`data-step`/`data-position` attributes are supported, while `scanAttributeTour` (packages/core/src/compat/intro-compat.ts:9-13) only reads `data-gf-step`/`data-gf-title`/`data-gf-body`/`data-gf-placement`; apps/docs/guide/vanilla.md:90 repeats the same false claim.
findings.fix: Correct both mapping tables to the real event names (`tour:complete`, `tour:abandon`, `step:skip`), `stop()`, and `spotlight.overlayOpacity`; delete the `allowDismiss` row. Either implement real `data-intro`/`data-step`/`data-position` aliases in intro-compat.ts (which would make the Intro.js migration claim true) or fix README.md:546 and vanilla.md:90 to show `data-gf-*`.
findings.verifierNote: Most sub-claims verified: TourEvents (types/index.ts:202-216) has tour:complete/tour:abandon but no `tour:end` or `tour:skip`; Step (53-72) has no `allowDismiss`; SpotlightOptions (121-133) declares `overlayOpacity`, not `opacity`, so migrate-driver.md:55 is a no-op; scanAttributeTour (intro-compat.ts:9-13) reads only data-gf-step/-title/-body/-placement, so README.md:544 and vanilla.md:90 are false. Two errors though: (1) `gf.end()` DOES work at runtime — TourEngine.end() is defined at tour.ts:159 and survives the Object.assign (index.ts:214), so it is only missing from the GuideFlowInstance type, not 'not exposed'; (2) the quoted row `stagePadding → config.spotlight.padding` is actually CORRECT — SpotlightOptions.padding exists at types/index.ts:122. So one of the three quoted evidence rows is not a defect.

findings.title: HTML sanitizer tests cover four benign payloads and none of the known regex bypasses
findings.evidence:

findings.fix: Add a table of ~20 XSS payloads (unclosed tags, mixed case, nested reconstruction, `<svg onload>`, `<math>`, unquoted and whitespace/entity-obfuscated `javascript:` URLs) asserting no dangerous node or attribute survives — parsing the sanitized output with DOMParser and walking it rather than substring-matching the string. findings.title: Persistence guide says ttl:0 disables expiry; it actually expires all progress immediately
findings.evidence: Set `ttl: 0` to disable expiry (progress persists indefinitely).
findings.impact: packages/core/src/persistence/progress-store.ts:95 is `this._ttl = config.ttl ?? DEFAULT_TTL` — nullish coalescing, so `0` is kept, not replaced. `saveSnapshot` then writes `expiresAt: Date.now() + 0` (line 104) and `loadSnapshot` evicts on `if (Date.now() > entry.expiresAt)` (line 113). With `ttl: 0` every snapshot, every dismissal, and every completion record is discarded on the very next read — the exact opposite of the documented behaviour. A team that follows this guide to make onboarding state permanent instead makes it entirely non-persistent, and users are re-shown tours they already dismissed. Nothing tests this: progress-store.test.ts:136 only covers `ttl: 1`.
findings.fix: Either implement the documented semantics (`const ttl = config.ttl === 0 ? Infinity : config.ttl ?? DEFAULT_TTL`) or correct persistence.md:99 to say `ttl: 0` expires immediately and that `Infinity` is the way to disable expiry. Add a progress-store test for `ttl: 0` and for `ttl: Infinity`.
findings.verifierNote: persistence.md:101 (cited 99) reads `Set \`ttl: 0\` to disable expiry (progress persists indefinitely).` progress-store.ts:31 (cited 95) is `this._ttl = config.ttl ?? DEFAULT_TTL` — nullish coalescing preserves 0. Lines 40/67/98 write `expiresAt: Date.now() + this._ttl` and lines 49/76/110 evict on `Date.now() > entry.expiresAt`, so with ttl:0 every snapshot, dismissal and completion record is dropped on the next read (any read ≥1ms later). progress-store.test.ts:136 covers only ttl:1.

findings.title: AI output cannot reach core without a hand-written wrapper, and the documented 'validated against the actual DOM' step does not exist

findings.title: .changeset/ contains only config.json — zero changesets, so the release workflow can neither version nor publish anything
findings.evidence:
- name: Create Release PR or Publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@v1
findings.impact: `ls .changeset` returns config.json only, yet every package sits at 0.1.9 — versions were hand-bumped across at least four commits (d81e049, dbef294, 4d9604b) with no changeset files. changesets/action with no pending changesets opens no release PR and runs no publish, so release.yml has never actually published anything and never will until someone writes a changeset. Because the version bumps bypassed changesets, no CHANGELOG.md was ever generated for any package, and consumers get npm releases with no notes describing what changed between 0.1.6 and 0.1.9.
findings.fix: Either commit real changesets and let `changeset version` own the version numbers, or drop changesets and adopt an explicit release script. Add a CI gate that fails a PR touching packages/*/src with no .changeset/*.md file (already noted as missing in ci-has-no-e2e-size-coverage-or-changeset-gate) so the two can never diverge again.

findings.title: ExperimentEngine returns a variant that no GuideFlow API can apply — the advertised A/B testing changes nothing

findings.impact: GuideFlowConfig (packages/core/src/types/index.ts:234-248) accepts only renderer, persistence, context, spotlight, nonce, injectStyles and debug — there is no `theme`, no variant hook, and no flow-selection API. Fix packages/analytics/src/index.ts:42 and rewrite apps/docs/guide/ab-testing.md's 'Use the variant' block.

findings.title: Playwright declares a chromium/firefox/webkit/mobile matrix that has never run — no code in this repo has ever executed outside Chromium and happy-dom

projects: [

findings.title: Combined, the studio and the DevTools extension leave zero authoring path for anyone who cannot write TypeScript
findings.evidence:
::: warning Coming Soon
The DevTools extension is currently in development and not yet published to browser extension stores.
findings.impact: The README bullet 'CLI — scaffold configs, launch the visual studio, export flows' and the AI positioning both imply a visual authoring loop. In reality: `guideflow studio` is a bare Vite server injecting one boolean; the DevTools extension is private:true, unpublished, untested, has no packaged artifact, and its bridge aborts every targeted tour on any page it is installed on; and `guideflow export` cannot round-trip a .ts flow. Taken together there is no path from 'I want a tour' to 'a tour exists' that does not go through a developer writing a FlowDefinition by hand and redeploying. The no-code editor is the feature that decides the Userpilot/Appcues/Pendo/Chameleon bake-off, and GuideFlow has zero of it despite advertising two of it.
findings.fix: Choose one authoring surface and finish it. The DevTools panel's Builder tab is closest to working — fix the bridge DataCloneError, make Load/Export round-trip a real FlowDefinition, add a packaging step and CI artifact, and publish it. Then delete the `studio` command and its README/docs claims rather than shipping two half-built editors.

findings.title: No backend, no flow CMS, and no self-hosting story — a tour cannot be changed without a code deploy
findings.evidence: import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
findings.impact: `guideflow push` POSTs to https://api.guideflow.dev/v1/flows, a service with no implementation anywhere in the repo, no signup path, no documented key issuance, and no OpenAPI/schema definition. There is no server package, no docker-compose, no database schema, no auth model, and no flow-fetch client — nothing in @guideflow/core can load a FlowDefinition over the network at all. So the only way to author or edit a tour is to write TypeScript and redeploy the application. Every competitor's core value proposition is exactly the opposite: non-engineers change tours without a deploy. Marketing 'GuideFlow Cloud' in the README while shipping no backend and no self-hosting instructions is the single largest credibility gap in the project.
findings.fix: Either (a) remove the Cloud/push story until a backend exists, or (b) ship a minimal self-hostable flow store: a documented JSON schema, a `gf.loadFlows(url)` fetch client in core with caching and ETag support, and a reference Express/Hono server + docker-compose under a new packages/server. Whichever you choose, state it explicitly in README.md so the positioning matches reality.

findings.title: No checklists, NPS/surveys, banners, announcements, or resource centre — the entire non-tour adoption surface is absent
findings.evidence: export { createMachine } from './fsm/machine.js'
findings.impact: Core's export surface is exclusively tour machinery: FlowMachine, SpotlightOverlay, computePosition, TourEngine, HotspotManager, HintSystem, ProgressStore, BroadcastSync, drivers, I18nRegistry, DefaultRenderer, intro-compat, tokens, emitter, ssr, styles. A repo-wide grep for checklist, survey, nps, banner, announcement, and 'resource cent' returns zero product hits. Every named competitor ships onboarding checklists and in-app surveys as headline SKUs, and Pendo/Chameleon/Userpilot all ship resource centres. A buyer evaluating GuideFlow against them finds roughly 20% of the expected surface, which alone decides most adoption bake-offs.
findings.fix: Pick one adjacent primitive and build it properly on top of the existing FSM + persistence — an onboarding checklist is the highest-leverage (it reuses ProgressStore's completed flags and the existing renderer) and would let the project claim more than 'tour library'. Ship it as @guideflow/checklist rather than bloating core.

findings.title: FlowDefinition and FlowSnapshot carry no version, so editing a flow resumes returning users into a stale state/step index
findings.evidence:
export interface FlowSnapshot {
  flowId: string
  currentState: string
  stepIndex: number
  completed: boolean
  timestamp: number
findings.impact: ProgressStore keys snapshots on `${keyFn(userId)}:${flowId}:snapshot` (packages/core/src/persistence/progress-store.ts:36) with no version, hash, or step-count fingerprint. A developer who renames a state, deletes a step, or reorders steps and redeploys will have every returning user restored via machine.restore({ state, stepIndex }) into a state that may no longer exist or a stepIndex past the end of the new steps array — producing the stuck, invisible tour already noted as machine-restore-unvalidated, but now triggered by an ordinary content edit rather than tampering. Every competitor versions flows precisely because tour content churns weekly. There is also no way to migrate, expire, or invalidate progress on publish.
findings.fix: Add `version?: string | number` to FlowDefinition and persist it (plus a derived step-count/state-name fingerprint) on FlowSnapshot. In createGuideFlow's resume path (packages/core/src/index.ts:243-256), discard the snapshot and start fresh when the stored version/fingerprint does not match the flow being started.

findings.title: No scheduling, frequency capping, cooldown, or cross-flow orchestration — nothing stops several tours firing at once
findings.evidence: const key = `${this._keyFn(userId)}:${snapshot.flowId}:snapshot`
findings.impact: ProgressStore is strictly per-flow: it records a snapshot, a completed flag, and a dismissed flag for one flowId. There is no global 'last tour shown at' timestamp, no per-session counter, no cooldown, no start/end date on a flow, and no queue or priority when two flows both want to start. Calling start() twice silently abandons the running tour (per docs-tour-engine-start-throws). A product team running four onboarding tours has no way to say 'at most one per session' or 'not within 7 days of the last one' — the standard frequency-capping controls in every commercial tool — so shipping more than one or two flows produces an unusable experience.
findings.fix: Add global (not per-flow) counters to ProgressStore — lastShownAt, sessionShownCount — and a `frequency` block on FlowDefinition (maxPerSession, cooldownMs, startsAt/endsAt). Have createGuideFlow's start() consult them before _engineStart, and add an orchestrator that resolves competing flows by priority.

findings.title: Flows have no targeting, audience, URL, or trigger model — every tour must be started by imperative application code
findings.impact: There is no `audience`, `segment`, `urlPattern`, `trigger`, or `priority` field anywhere on FlowDefinition, and createGuideFlow exposes no rule evaluator — the only conditional mechanism in the whole engine is per-step `showIf`. Deciding *who* sees a tour, *where*, and *when* is therefore entirely the host application's problem, hand-written at every call site. Targeting rules are the primary product of Userpilot, Appcues, Pendo and Chameleon; without them GuideFlow is a tour renderer, not an onboarding platform, and cannot be adopted by the growth/PM buyer it markets to.
findings.fix: Add an optional `targeting` block to FlowDefinition (urlPattern, audience predicate over GuidanceContext, startTrigger: 'manual' | 'load' | 'selector' | 'event') and a `gf.evaluate()` / `gf.autoStart()` entry point that picks the highest-priority matching flow. Document it as a first-class guide page.

findings.title: Every persistence feature silently no-ops unless the caller supplies context.userId, which no quick-start does
findings.evidence:
const userId = _config.context?.userId
      if (userId) {
findings.impact: Resume, completion gating, dismissal, and cross-tab BroadcastSync are all inside `if (userId)`, and tour:complete only persists when `_config.context?.userId` is set (index.ts:196-201). Core never generates or stores an anonymous device id, and there is no `anonymousId` option. The README quick start, apps/docs/guide/quick-start.md, and the CLI's generated guideflow.ts all call createGuideFlow() with no context, so the four features the README lists under 'Persistent progress' are dead by default and fail silently — no warning is logged. Every competitor falls back to an anonymous device id precisely because most onboarding tours run before login.
findings.fix: Generate and persist an anonymous id (crypto.randomUUID stored under gf:anon-id) when context.userId is absent, expose it as `gf.anonymousId`, and use it as the ProgressStore key fallback. At minimum, warn once in debug mode when persistence is configured but no userId is available.

findings.title: window.__guideflow is the DevTools extension's entire integration contract and core never sets it, nor do the docs mention it

findings.impact: bridge.ts:79, :128 and :196, plus content/inspector.ts:6 and :313, all key off window.__guideflow. createGuideFlow() in packages/core/src/index.ts never assigns it, and apps/docs/packages/devtools.md — the only user-facing devtools page — never mentions the global. The extension's one advertised feature is unreachable for every real integration.
