findings.title: The deprecated `guideflow` proxy silently discards property writes
findings.impact: `receiver` is the proxy, not the singleton, so `Reflect.set` performs the final CreateDataProperty on the *receiver* — the proxy's empty `{}` target — instead of on the instance. `guideflow.i18n = myRegistry` therefore returns `true`, mutates nothing on the real instance, and a later read (`get` forwards to `Reflect.get(getGuideFlow(), prop, receiver)`) still returns the original registry, so the write vanishes with no error. Any assignment through the documented CDN/script-tag singleton is silently lost.
findings.fix: Drop `receiver` from both traps: `Reflect.set(getGuideFlow(), prop, value)` and `Reflect.get(getGuideFlow(), prop)` (the latter also avoids invoking prototype getters with the proxy as `this`). Or remove the proxy entirely in favour of `getGuideFlow()`.
findings.verifierNote: index.ts:365-367 verbatim. Reflect.set(target, prop, value, receiver) performs OrdinarySet on the singleton but completes with CreateDataProperty on the *receiver*, which here is the proxy (index.ts:360) whose target is `{}` and which has no defineProperty trap — so the value lands on the throwaway object and returns true. The get trap at 361-364 reads from getGuideFlow(), not the proxy target, so the write is unobservable afterwards. For prototype getters like isActive the set would instead fail silently/throw in strict mode; either way the assignment never reaches the instance.

findings.title: restore() accepts an out-of-range or malformed stepIndex from untrusted storage, producing a stuck invisible tour
findings.evidence:
restore(snapshot: { state: string; stepIndex: number; context?: TContext }): void {
    if (!(snapshot.state in this._ctx.flow.states)) return
    this._ctx.currentState = snapshot.state
    this._ctx.stepIndex = snapshot.stepIndex
findings.impact: Only `state` is validated. `stepIndex` is written verbatim, so a snapshot saved against an older build of the flow (state now has fewer steps) or hand-edited localStorage yields `currentStep === null` and a tour that is `isActive` but renders nothing (see fsm-send-to-nonexistent-state for the same dead end). The value is fully untrusted: `LocalStorageDriver.get` does `JSON.parse(raw) as T` (drivers.ts:17) with no shape check, and `ProgressStore.loadSnapshot` only compares `Date.now() > entry.expiresAt` — for a tampered entry without `expiresAt` that comparison is `false`, so a payload such as `{"value":{"currentState":"welcome","stepIndex":"9e99"}}` is accepted and returned as a `FlowSnapshot`. `restore()` also silently ignores its own `state` rejection, so a stale snapshot for a renamed state leaves the tour on step 0 with no diagnostic.
findings.fix: Clamp and validate: `this._ctx.stepIndex = Math.min(Math.max(0, Math.trunc(Number(snapshot.stepIndex) || 0)), Math.max(0, steps.length - 1))`, return a boolean so callers can detect rejection, and add a `isFlowSnapshot(v): v is FlowSnapshot` runtime guard in `ProgressStore.loadSnapshot` that discards (and removes) entries failing validation, including entries with a non-numeric or missing `expiresAt`.
findings.verifierNote: machine.ts:139-142 verbatim — only `state` is checked; stepIndex is assigned unvalidated, and LocalStorageDriver.get does `JSON.parse(raw) as T` with no shape check (drivers.ts:17) while loadSnapshot's only gate is `Date.now() > entry.expiresAt` (progress-store.ts:49), which is false for a tampered entry lacking expiresAt. The missing validation is real. But the stated impact is derivative and overstated: on the resume path restore() is never followed by a render at all (index.ts:250-252), so the visible symptom is the stale step-0 popover from the resume bug; an out-of-range index only degrades later next()/prev() calls (nextStep falls through to send('NEXT')) rather than producing the described stuck invisible tour. Requires storage tampering or a flow-shape change across deploys.

findings.title: Per-step spotlight `padding` permanently mutates the overlay options and leaks into all later steps
findings.impact: `SpotlightOverlay.show()` merges the per-call options into its persistent `_options`. `TourEngine._renderCurrentStep` calls `show(target, { ...this._options.spotlight, ...(step.padding !== undefined && { padding: step.padding }) })` (tour.ts:245-248) — when a step omits `padding`, the spread contributes no `padding` key, so the previous step's override survives. A flow with `padding: 40` on step 2 renders steps 3..n with a 40px cutout instead of the configured default (or the built-in 8). The same leak applies to `borderRadius`, `overlayOpacity`, `animated` and `dismissOnBackdropClick` if a caller ever passes them per-call.
findings.fix: Do not mutate instance state from `show()`: keep `_defaults` immutable and compute an effective option set per call (`const opts = { ...this._defaults, ...options }`) used by `_update()`, or have TourEngine always pass a fully-resolved object including an explicit `padding: step.padding ?? this._options.spotlight?.padding ?? 8`.
findings.verifierNote: spotlight.ts:76-78 verbatim — show() merges per-call options into the persistent `_options`. tour.ts:245-248 spreads `...this._options.spotlight` then conditionally adds padding, so when no global spotlight config is supplied `this._options.spotlight` is undefined, the object is `{}`, the `if (options)` branch still runs and leaves the previous step's padding in place for all later steps. Note the finding overstates one case: if the app configures `spotlight: { padding: n }`, that key is respread each time and does reset. Downgrading to P2 — visual-only regression in later steps, not a functional break.

findings.title: Popover steals focus with no focus trap and never restores it; aria-labelledby dangles when the step has no title
findings.impact: The element declares `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` (lines 94-95) — which tells screen readers the rest of the page is inert — but there is no focus trap: Tab walks straight out of the popover into page content that the overlay makes unclickable, so keyboard and screen-reader users can focus controls they cannot activate. `hideStep()` removes the node from the DOM (line 130) without restoring focus to whatever was focused before the tour, so focus falls back to `<body>` after every step transition and at tour end — a WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) failure and a common screen-reader dead end. Separately, `aria-labelledby="${id}-title"` / `aria-describedby="${id}-body"` are set unconditionally (lines 96-97) but the referenced nodes only exist when `content.title` / `content.body`|`html` are present (lines 174, 178-180), leaving dangling IDREFs and an unlabelled dialog for steps without a title.
findings.fix: Record `document.activeElement` in `renderStep` before focusing, restore it in `hideStep()`; add a keydown trap on the popover cycling Tab/Shift+Tab within its focusable set; and set `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` only when the corresponding node is emitted (falling back to `aria-label`).
findings.verifierNote: default-renderer.ts:121-125 verbatim. role='dialog' and aria-modal='true' are set at lines 94-95, yet the class contains no keydown/Tab handling at all, so focus can leave the popover into the overlay-blocked page. hideStep (128-133) removes the node with no saved/restored previous activeElement. aria-labelledby/aria-describedby are set unconditionally at 96-97 while the `${id}-title` node exists only when content.title is present (line 174) and `${id}-body` only when body or html is present (177-181), leaving dangling IDREFs.

findings.title: A step whose target selector matches nothing silently becomes a full-screen dark modal with no warning
findings.impact: A typo'd or not-yet-mounted selector returns `null`, which is indistinguishable from the intentional "floating/modal step" case (`target?: string | HTMLElement | null`, types/index.ts:55). The spotlight then takes its no-target branch and paints the whole viewport with `rgba(0,0,0,opacity)` (spotlight.ts:179-192) and the popover centres itself — the app appears to be covered by an unexplained dark modal. Nothing is logged (`_log` only fires when `debug: true`, tour.ts:367-372) and no event is emitted, so the most common authoring mistake in a tour library produces a confusing UI with zero diagnostics. There is also no retry/wait for elements that mount asynchronously, which is the norm in SPA onboarding.
findings.fix: Distinguish the cases: when `typeof step.target === 'string'` and `querySelector` returns null, `console.warn` (unconditionally, once per step) and emit a dedicated event (e.g. `step:target-missing`); optionally poll/`MutationObserver`-wait for a configurable timeout before falling back, and let the step opt into skip-if-missing behaviour.
findings.verifierNote: tour.ts:283-290 verbatim — a non-matching selector returns null, identical to the intentional floating-step case (`target?: string | HTMLElement | null`, types/index.ts:55). SpotlightOverlay._update then takes the no-target branch (spotlight.ts:179-192) and sets `background: rgba(0,0,0,${opacity})` on the full-viewport overlay, while DefaultRenderer._position centres the popover (default-renderer.ts:204-210). Nothing logs (_log is gated on debug, tour.ts:367-372) and no tour:error is emitted; there is no retry/wait loop anywhere in _resolveTarget.

findings.title: Style injection is keyed by a module-global id set, so destroying one instance strips styles from other live instances (and the popover CSS is never removed)
findings.impact: `SpotlightOverlay.destroy()` calls `removeStyles(SPOTLIGHT_CSS_ID)` (spotlight.ts:110), which deletes the single shared `<style data-gf="gf-spotlight">` element. With two GuideFlow instances (a documented multi-tenant/embedded scenario, and what `getGuideFlow()` plus an explicit `createGuideFlow()` produces), destroying the first leaves the second's overlay unstyled mid-tour. Conversely `DefaultRenderer` has no `destroy()` at all, so `gf-popover-renderer` styles stay in `<head>` forever after `instance.destroy()` while `injectedIds` still contains the id — a subsequent instance created with a CSP `nonce` gets no `<style>` re-injected and its inline styles are blocked. `configure({nonce})` has the same hole: hotspot/hint styles already injected without a nonce are never re-injected with it.
findings.fix: Reference-count injections per id (increment on inject, only remove at zero) or scope injection per instance id; give `DefaultRenderer` a `destroy()` that calls `removeStyles(POPOVER_CSS_ID)` and is invoked from `createGuideFlow().destroy()`; and re-inject when the nonce changes for an id.
findings.verifierNote: styles.ts:8-14 verbatim — `injectedIds` is a module-level Set and removeStyles (22-28) deletes every matching style element plus the id. SpotlightOverlay.destroy calls removeStyles(SPOTLIGHT_CSS_ID) at spotlight.ts:110, and SPOTLIGHT_CSS_ID is a single shared constant, so destroying one instance strips the CSS a second live instance depends on. DefaultRenderer has no destroy/removeStyles (searched the whole class), so gf-popover-renderer stays registered in injectedIds forever and a later nonce'd injectStyles returns early at line 12.

findings.title: `totalSteps` / progress counter are per-state, contradicting the documented "total steps in the active flow"

findings.title: Step action/variant and i18n strings are interpolated into HTML attributes without escaping

${actions.map((a) => `

              ${this._esc(a.label)}

findings.title: startRecording unconditionally creates and appends a new badge, leaking the previous one into the page DOM

findings.title: Export writes StepDraft[] under a `steps` key, not a FlowDefinition — the exported file cannot be fed to GuideFlow

So the advertised "Export — generate flow definitions from visual recordings" (apps/docs/packages/devtools.md:19) produces a file that `guideflow.start()` rejects, and `guideflow.createFlow()` cannot consume. The panel's own runTour (423-443) builds the correct shape, so the two disagree. findings.title: Manifest declares only a service_worker background and the code uses promise-returning chrome.* APIs — the extension cannot run in Firefox
findings.impact: Firefox's MV3 implementation does not support `background.service_worker`; it requires `background.scripts` (event pages), and there is no `browser_specific_settings.gecko` block, so the extension will not load. Even if it did, the code assumes promise-returning `chrome.*`, which is a Chrome-only behaviour — Firefox's `chrome` namespace is callback-only and only `browser.*` returns promises. Concretely, `chrome.tabs.sendMessage(tab.id, {...}).catch(() => {})` (service-worker.ts:67-69) and `await chrome.tabs.query({ active: true, currentWindow: true })` (popup.tsx:224) would throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'catch')` / return `undefined`. Meanwhile apps/docs/packages/index.md:36 advertises this as a "Chrome/Firefox extension".
findings.fix: Either drop the Firefox claim from the docs, or add a `webextension-polyfill` dependency, switch all call sites to `browser.*`, add `background.scripts` + `browser_specific_settings.gecko.id` to a Firefox-specific manifest, and add a `build:firefox` script. Also add `minimum_chrome_version` so Chrome/Edge installs fail loudly rather than at runtime.
findings.verifierNote: manifest.json:18-21 declares only `background.service_worker` and the file has no `browser_specific_settings` block. Promise-style chrome.* usage confirmed at service-worker.ts:67-69 (`.catch(() => {})` on chrome.tabs.sendMessage) and popup.tsx:224/230/266/272 (`await chrome.*`). apps/docs/packages/index.md:36 does say 'Chrome/Firefox extension'. Downgrading to P2: the package is private, unpublished, and documented as 'Coming Soon', so this is an unmet doc claim plus a porting gap, not a shipped break.

findings.title: Import silently ignores invalid JSON and applies unvalidated step objects
findings.impact: Pick the wrong file and nothing happens at all — no error, no message, the Import button just appears broken. When the JSON *is* valid but not a GuideFlow export, `Array.isArray(data.steps)` is the only check: step objects with no `id` become React keys of `undefined` (duplicate-key warnings and wrong rows re-rendering), `removeStep(id)` filters on `s.id !== undefined` and deletes every id-less step at once, and `step.placement`/`step.target` of the wrong type flow straight into the generated flow. There is also no `reader.onerror` handler, so a read failure is equally invisible.
findings.fix: Validate the parsed object against the StepDraft shape (require `id` and `title`, coerce/backfill missing ids with `crypto.randomUUID()`), render a visible error banner in both the catch and an added `reader.onerror`, and report how many steps were imported.
findings.verifierNote: app.tsx:470-489 verbatim; the only guard is `Array.isArray(data.steps)` and the catch is an empty comment, with no `reader.onerror`. Verified the downstream consequences: `key={step.id}` at line 657 and `removeStep(id)` at 394-396 filtering `s.id !== id` would delete every id-less step at once when id is undefined.

findings.title: injectBridge marks itself done before the script loads and ignores onerror, making any load failure permanent and silent
findings.impact: `bridgeInjected = true` is set before the network/CSP outcome is known, and there is no `script.onerror` handler. If the injection fails for any reason — a page CSP that rejects the extension-origin script, the extension being reloaded so `chrome.runtime.getURL` yields a dead origin, or `document.head`/`documentElement` not yet available — the guard permanently blocks every retry, including the explicit re-injection on `GF_DEVTOOLS_OPEN` (line 311). The panel then reports "not detected" forever on that page with no diagnostic, and the user's only recourse is a reload they have no reason to try. `run_at: "document_idle"` compounds this: any tour that auto-starts on page load emits its events before the bridge subscribes, and those events are lost with no backfill.
findings.fix: Set `bridgeInjected = true` in `onload` and add `script.onerror = () => { bridgeInjected = false; send({ type: 'GF_BRIDGE_INJECT_FAILED' }); }` so the panel can render an actionable error. Move the content script to `run_at: "document_start"`, and prefer `chrome.scripting.registerContentScripts` with `world: 'MAIN'` over `<script>` injection to remove the page-CSP dependency entirely.
findings.verifierNote: inspector.ts:41-51 verbatim — `bridgeInjected = true` on line 43 precedes appendChild on line 50, and only `onload` is wired, never `onerror`. inspector.ts:309-317 (GF_DEVTOOLS_OPEN) calls injectBridge() again, which the flag short-circuits, so the documented recovery path is dead for that page load. run_at is document_idle per manifest.json:26, so early auto-start events are missed with no backfill.

findings.title: Content script does not set all_frames, so GuideFlow running in any iframe is invisible and unpickable
findings.impact: `all_frames` defaults to false, so the content script and its bridge are injected only into the top frame. Any product that renders GuideFlow inside an iframe — embedded apps, Storybook's preview iframe (which this very monorepo ships as apps/storybook), design-tool embeds, checkout widgets — reports "not detected" with no explanation. Element picking cannot cross into an iframe either, and there is no per-frame routing in the service worker (`sender.tab.id` collapses all frames of a tab onto one port, so even with `all_frames: true` the panel could not tell frames apart). `match_about_blank` is also absent, so `srcdoc`/`about:blank` frames are excluded.
findings.fix: Add `"all_frames": true` and `"match_about_blank": true`, key the service worker's routing on `${tabId}:${sender.frameId}`, and add a frame selector to the panel header so the user can choose which frame to inspect. At minimum, detect the top-frame-only limitation and show "GuideFlow may be running in an iframe — not supported" in the empty state.
findings.verifierNote: manifest.json:22-28 verbatim; no `all_frames` and no `match_about_blank`, so both default to false and injection is top-frame only. The service worker keys everything on `sender.tab?.id` (service-worker.ts:105) with no frameId, so per-frame routing genuinely does not exist. Downgrading to P2: all_frames:false is the platform default and a common deliberate choice; this is a coverage gap, not a defect on the supported path.

findings.title: private:true with no zip/web-ext packaging step and no CI artifact — there is no supported way to install the extension
findings.evidence: "private": true,
findings.impact: `private: true` excludes the package from the changesets publish in .github/workflows/release.yml, and neither workflow produces an extension artifact (grepping `.github/` for "devtools" returns nothing). There is no `zip`/`web-ext build`/`crx` script, no `.crx`/`.zip` upload step, and no store listing assets — `packages/devtools/assets/` contains only `icon-16.png`, `icon-48.png`, `icon-128.png`, with no 440x280 or 1280x800 promo tiles or screenshots that the Chrome Web Store requires. The only documented install path is "clone the repo, run pnpm build, Load unpacked" (apps/docs/packages/devtools.md:30-39), which forces every user to have pnpm and the full monorepo, and means unpacked installs get no auto-updates.
findings.fix: Add a `"package": "vite build && cd dist && zip -r ../guideflow-devtools-$npm_package_version.zip ."` script, add an `actions/upload-artifact` step to ci.yml so every commit produces an installable zip, and add store-listing assets (screenshots, promo tile, privacy-policy URL) under `packages/devtools/store/` before claiming store availability anywhere in the docs.
findings.verifierNote: Facts check out: `"private": true` is present (package.json line 5, not 6 as cited), assets/ contains exactly icon-16/48/128.png, no zip/web-ext/crx script, and grep of .github/ for 'devtools' returns nothing while release.yml only runs changesets publish. But the headline 'there is no supported way to install' is wrong — Load-unpacked is a real, documented install path (apps/docs/packages/devtools.md), and the package is explicitly documented as not yet store-published, so the absence of store assets is current design, not an oversight. P2.

findings.title: Panel controls are not keyboard operable: inline edit via <strong onClick>, drag-only reordering, unlabelled icon buttons, non-semantic toggle and tabs
findings.evidence: startEdit(i)} title="Click to edit" > {step.title}
findings.impact: A `<strong>` is not focusable and has no key handler, so a keyboard user can never rename a step. Step reordering exists only through HTML5 drag events (`draggable` + `onDragStart`/`onDragOver`, lines 659-662) with no keyboard alternative. The delete button at lines 692-697 renders only the glyph `✕` with no `aria-label` and no `title`, so a screen reader announces "button" — and it sits next to the identically-shaped 👁 preview button. `Toggle` (lines 308-318) is a bare `<button>` with `aria-label={on ? 'Turn off' : 'Turn on'}` but no `role="switch"`/`aria-checked`, so state is conveyed only by colour. None of the buttons in the file set `type="button"`. The tab strip (lines 1214-1222) uses plain buttons with no `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`/`aria-selected` and no arrow-key navigation, and the emoji labels have no text alternative. This is notable given apps/docs/index.md:42 advertises "ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, focus management … out of the box".
findings.fix: Replace the `<strong>` with a focusable button (or double-click-to-edit plus an explicit edit button), add ↑/↓ move buttons alongside drag, give every icon button an `aria-label`, convert `Toggle` to `role="switch" aria-checked={on}`, add `type="button"` everywhere, and give the tab strip proper `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`/`aria-selected` with arrow-key handling.
findings.verifierNote: All sub-claims verified: `<strong onClick>` at app.tsx:677-684 (not focusable, no key handler); drag-only reorder at 659-662 with no keyboard path; the ✕ button at 692-697 has neither aria-label nor title while the adjacent 👁 at 685-691 has only a title; Toggle at 308-318 is a bare button with aria-label and no role="switch"/aria-checked; `grep -c 'type="button"' app.tsx` returns 0; the tab strip at 1214-1222 uses plain buttons with no tablist/tab/aria-selected. apps/docs/index.md:42 does make the accessibility claim (about the library, which the finding acknowledges).

findings.title: The panel's active-tour progress bar can never render — GF_GET_ACTIVE_TOUR is never sent
findings.impact: `activeTour` is only ever set from a `GF_ACTIVE_TOUR_STATE` message, which `bridge.ts:159-172` emits only in response to a `GF_GET_ACTIVE_TOUR` command. Grepping the package shows `GF_GET_ACTIVE_TOUR` exists solely as a handler in bridge.ts:159 and a forwarder in inspector.ts:406 — no panel or popup code ever sends it, and there is no polling interval. Therefore `activeTour` is permanently `null`, and the entire header progress-bar block (app.tsx:1201-1210), the `progressPct` computation (1186-1189), and the `ActiveTourState` interface are dead code. Users get no live step position in the panel despite the UI being built for it.
findings.fix: Send `sendToContent({ type: 'GF_GET_ACTIVE_TOUR' })` on panel mount and on every `GF_TOUR_EVENT` (or on a 500 ms interval while `detected`), and reset `activeTour` to null on `tour:complete`/`tour:abandon`.
findings.verifierNote: Grep confirms GF_GET_ACTIVE_TOUR exists only as bridge.ts:159 (handler) and inspector.ts:406 (forwarder); no send site in app.tsx or popup.tsx and no polling. `activeTour` is set only at app.tsx:1162-1163, so it stays null and the header block at 1201-1210 plus `progressPct` (1186-1189) are dead. Confirmed, but it is unreachable UI rather than a broken shipped path: P2.

findings.title: Every panel→page command swallows its error, so the panel has no "content script unavailable" state
findings.impact: This one function backs Pick, Run, Highlight, Start/Stop Recording, Set Debug, and the mount-time `GF_DEVTOOLS_OPEN` probe. Every failure is discarded. On a page where the content script cannot run — `chrome://` pages, the Web Store, PDF viewer, a page loaded before the extension was installed or reloaded, or any frame the content script did not match — all six buttons become silent no-ops with the panel still reporting a normal UI. Chrome documents DevTools extension pages as having access to only a subset of the extension APIs (message the background page for the rest), and this bypasses the per-tab `devtoolsPorts` relay the worker already implements for exactly this purpose; if `chrome.tabs` is unavailable the `.catch` itself throws a TypeError on `undefined`. Either way the user gets no diagnostic.
findings.fix: Route panel→page commands through the existing background port (`port.postMessage`) and let the service worker call `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`, replying with a delivery result. Track a `contentScriptAlive` flag in the panel and render a blocking banner ("Reload the page to connect the GuideFlow inspector") with a reload button when delivery fails.
findings.verifierNote: app.tsx:263-268 verbatim, and it does back GF_START/STOP_INSPECT (369,372), GF_START_TOUR (444,899), GF_HIGHLIGHT_SELECTOR (493), GF_START/STOP_RECORDING (1098,1102), GF_SET_DEBUG (1083) and the mount probe (1176) — every one silent on failure, with no 'content script unavailable' state anywhere in the file. One sub-claim is unproven: chrome.tabs is in practice reachable from DevTools extension pages in current Chrome, so the 'the .catch itself throws a TypeError' scenario is speculative. The primary defect stands.

findings.title: Popup "DevTools" and "Refresh" buttons produce no visible effect
findings.impact: The button is labelled "🛠 DevTools" with the tooltip "Open DevTools panel for advanced features", and the code comment acknowledges it cannot open DevTools — but it never actually instructs the user either. Clicking it just closes the popup, which reads as a broken button. The "↻ Refresh" button (lines 398-406) has the same problem from the other direction: it sends `GF_LIST_FLOWS`, whose result travels bridge → content → worker → `devtoolsPorts` and is delivered only to an open DevTools panel — the popup never receives `GF_FLOWS_LIST` and has no flows UI to render it into. Two of the popup's four Quick Actions do nothing observable.
findings.fix: Replace the DevTools button with inline text ("Press F12 and open the GuideFlow tab") or a link to the docs, and either give the popup a flows list fed by a `GF_GET_FLOWS` request/response through the worker, or remove the Refresh button.
findings.verifierNote: popup.tsx:318-324 verbatim, including the comment admitting DevTools cannot be opened programmatically, with no user-facing instruction — it just closes. Refresh at 397-406 sends GF_LIST_FLOWS, whose GF_FLOWS_LIST reply is routed only to devtoolsPorts (service-worker.ts:149-153); the popup has no runtime.onMessage listener and no flows UI, so it can never render the result.

findings.title: Popup disables Pick Element and Record on `!state.detected`, even though neither feature needs GuideFlow on the page
findings.impact: Element picking and interaction recording are implemented entirely in the content script (`startInspect`/`startRecording` in inspector.ts) and never touch `window.__guideflow`. Gating them on `state.detected` — a flag that is wrong most of the time because it dies with the service worker (see mv3-state-dies-on-suspend) — means the popup's two headline actions are greyed out on pages where they would work perfectly. The whole "build a tour on a page that doesn't have GuideFlow yet" use case, which is the primary reason to have a visual builder, is blocked.
findings.fix: Drop `disabled={!state.detected}` from the Pick Element and Record buttons (popup.tsx:377, 385) and keep the gate only on flow-execution actions (Run tour). Show the detection dot as informational, not as a permission.
findings.verifierNote: Evidence verbatim (popup.tsx:376-378, same pattern at 386). Correct that startInspect/startRecording (inspector.ts:287-301, 193-200) never touch `window.__guideflow`. But this is a defensible product decision for a GuideFlow-branded extension, and the 'primary reason to have a visual builder' framing is an assertion, not a defect proof — Run/Preview genuinely do need the page global. Real but overstated: P2.

findings.title: Input recording listens for `change`, missing typed values that never blur, and captures raw field values
findings.evidence:
document.addEventListener('click', onRecordClick, true);
  document.addEventListener('change', onRecordInput, true);
findings.impact: `change` fires only on commit (blur for text inputs), so a user who types into a field and then clicks the next element gets an ordering that does not match what they did, and a user who types and then navigates gets nothing recorded. Nothing else is captured at all — no keyboard navigation, no scrolling, no hover, no `submit`, no route changes — so a "recording" of a realistic flow is a bare list of click targets. There is no debouncing or de-duplication either, so a double-click on one button produces two identical steps. `onRecordInput` also copies `(target as HTMLInputElement).value?.slice(0, 100)` into the recorded step (line 187) with no field-type filtering.
findings.fix: Listen to `input` (debounced ~400 ms per element) in addition to `change`, add `submit` and `chrome.webNavigation`/`popstate` markers so multi-page flows are representable, de-duplicate consecutive identical selectors, and skip value capture for `type="password"`, `autocomplete="cc-*"`, and `[data-sensitive]` fields.
findings.verifierNote: inspector.ts:197-198 verbatim (click + change, both capture). `change` semantics are as described, and inspector.ts:187 does copy `(target as HTMLInputElement).value?.slice(0,100)` into the message with no type filter — password/credit-card fields included. Only click and change are registered; no submit/keydown/scroll/route-change capture and no dedupe anywhere in the file.

findings.title: Recording and inspect state live in content-script module scope and die on every navigation, with no persistence and no UI resync
findings.evidence:
let recordingMode = false;
let recordingBadge: HTMLDivElement | null = null;
findings.impact: A page navigation or reload destroys the content script's globals. The "Recording…" badge disappears, click/change listeners are gone, and nothing tells the panel — `App.recording` stays true (app.tsx:1036) so the button still reads "⏹ Stop Rec" and the user keeps clicking, recording nothing. This makes multi-page tours — the single most common real onboarding shape (signup → dashboard → settings) — impossible to record. The same applies to `inspectMode` (line 95) and `bridgeInjected` (line 39). Recorded steps in the panel are likewise React state only, so closing DevTools discards them, and the builder's `steps` array (app.tsx:340) is lost with it — a half-built 15-step tour vanishes if the panel is closed.
findings.fix: Persist `recordingMode` to `chrome.storage.session` keyed by tabId and re-arm listeners at content-script start when the flag is set; persist accumulated recorded steps and the builder draft (`steps` + `flowName`) to `chrome.storage.local` on every mutation and rehydrate on panel mount. Listen for `chrome.tabs.onUpdated` in the service worker to re-issue `GF_START_RECORDING` after navigation.
findings.verifierNote: inspector.ts:103-104 (recordingMode/recordingBadge), :95 (inspectMode) and :39 (bridgeInjected) are all module-scope and reset on every content-script reload; nothing writes them to storage and nothing notifies the panel. app.tsx:1036 `recording` is only cleared by an explicit GF_RECORDING_STOPPED (1159-1161), which navigation never sends. Builder `steps` (app.tsx:340) and `recordedSteps` (1037) are React state only.

findings.title: Saving a tour gives no confirmation and does not refresh the saved-tours list
findings.impact: The service worker's `GF_SAVE_FLOW` handler does respond `{ ok: true, key }` (service-worker.ts:179), but the panel discards the response and swallows every error with `.catch(() => {})`. No toast, no state change, and crucially no call to `loadSavedTours()` — so after clicking 💾 Save the Flows tab still shows the old list and the Settings tab still shows the old "N tours stored locally" count until the panel is remounted. Users cannot tell whether the save succeeded, and the natural reaction (clicking Save repeatedly) silently overwrites the same key because `id` is derived from the tour name. Saving with an empty name generates a fresh `tour-${Date.now()}` id each time, quietly creating duplicate entries.
findings.fix: Await the response, call `loadSavedTours()` on `{ ok: true }`, and show an inline confirmation. Detect an existing `gf_flow_${id}` before writing and prompt "Overwrite existing tour 'X'?" instead of clobbering.
findings.verifierNote: app.tsx:447-453 verbatim; the response promise is discarded and `.catch(() => {})` swallows failures. `loadSavedTours` (1044-1059) lives in App and is never passed into BuilderTab (props 324-337), so no refresh path exists. The service worker does reply `{ok:true,key}` (service-worker.ts:179), and the key is derived from the id (175), so re-saves overwrite while empty names mint a new `tour-${Date.now()}` each time.

findings.title: aria-label and data-testid shortcuts return immediately without checking the selector matches exactly one element
findings.impact: Neither attribute is unique by nature. A table with ten rows each containing `<button aria-label="Delete">` yields the identical selector `[aria-label="Delete"]` for every row, and the generated tour step will always spotlight row 1. Same for repeated `data-testid` values in list components. There is also no `id` uniqueness/stability check on the preceding line 237 (`if (el.id) return '#' + CSS.escape(el.id)`) — React 18 `useId` and Radix produce ids like `:r3:` and `radix-:r7:` that change on every mount, so the selector is dead after the next render. Additionally `CSS.escape` is specified for CSS *identifiers*, not for quoted attribute-value strings; using it inside `"…"` produces escape sequences that are not the intended quoting mechanism.
findings.fix: After building any candidate, verify `document.querySelectorAll(candidate).length === 1` and fall through to the next strategy (or append a scoping ancestor / `:nth-of-type`) when it fails. Reject auto-generated ids by regex (`/^(:r[0-9a-z]+:|radix-|mui-|headlessui-)/`). For attribute values use `JSON.stringify(value)` to produce a correctly quoted CSS string rather than `CSS.escape`.
findings.verifierNote: inspector.ts:237-241 verbatim; all three shortcuts return on first match with no uniqueness check. The CSS.escape sub-claim is the weakest part — escaping inside a quoted attribute value still parses correctly in CSS (e.g. `"Delete\ Item"` resolves to the same string), so it is stylistic, not a functional break. The non-uniqueness and unstable-generated-id concerns hold. Scoping to P2 given the CSS.escape rationale does not survive.

findings.title: buildSelector walks parentElement only, so shadow-DOM elements yield selectors that document.querySelector can never resolve
findings.impact: `parentElement` is `null` at a shadow root boundary, so the walk terminates inside the shadow tree and returns a path rooted at the shadow root — e.g. `div:nth-child(1) > button:nth-child(2)` — which `document.querySelector` resolves against the light DOM and either misses or matches an unrelated node. Worse, the picker's listeners are on `document` in capture phase (`document.addEventListener('mouseover', onMouseOver, true)`, line 290), so for open shadow roots `e.target` is retargeted to the *host*, and for closed roots it is always the host: you can never actually pick an element inside a web component. Any app built on Lit, Stencil, Ionic, Shoelace, or Salesforce LWC is unpickable, and `GF_HIGHLIGHT_SELECTOR`'s `document.querySelector` (line 339) cannot pierce shadow boundaries either.
findings.fix: Use `e.composedPath()[0]` instead of `e.target` to get the true innermost node, walk `node.parentNode` and cross `ShadowRoot` boundaries via `.host`, and emit a structured selector (an array of per-root selector segments) that the highlighter resolves by chaining `.shadowRoot.querySelector`. At minimum, detect a shadow boundary and surface "element is inside a shadow root — not supported" instead of returning a broken selector.
findings.verifierNote: inspector.ts:254 walks `cur.parentElement`, which is null at a shadow root, and the picker listeners are on `document` in capture phase (290-291) — event retargeting means `e.target` is the host for both open and closed shadow roots, so shadow-internal elements genuinely cannot be picked. GF_HIGHLIGHT_SELECTOR's `document.querySelector` (339) also cannot pierce. Real gap, but it is an unsupported-scenario gap rather than a defect on the mainline path: P2.

findings.title: Service worker reads tour:start args as the flow object, so the popup always shows "unknown" and "Step 1/1"
findings.impact: Core emits `this.emit('tour:start', { flowId: flow.id })` (packages/core/src/engine/tour.ts:105) — the payload is `{ flowId }`, not the flow. So `args[0].id` is `undefined` → `flowId` is always the literal string `'unknown'`, and `args[0].steps` is `undefined` → `totalSteps` is always `1`. The subsequent `step:enter` branch then does `Math.min(tour.stepIndex + 1, tour.totalSteps - 1)` = `Math.min(n, 0)` = 0 forever. The popup's Active Tour card (popup.tsx:350-368) therefore always reads flow "unknown", "Step 1/1", and "100%", for every tour, regardless of length or position.
findings.fix: Read `evt.args?.[0]?.flowId` for the id. For step count, subscribe to `step:enter`'s `{ stepIndex }` and query `gf.totalSteps` via a `GF_GET_ACTIVE_TOUR` round trip rather than inferring from `tour:start`, and set `stepIndex` from the event payload instead of incrementing a counter (the current counter also never decrements on `prev()`).
findings.verifierNote: core/src/engine/tour.ts:105 is `this.emit('tour:start', { flowId: flow.id })`, so `args[0].id` and `args[0].steps` are both undefined against service-worker.ts:128-134 → flowId 'unknown', totalSteps 1. The step:enter branch (138) then computes `Math.min(stepIndex+1, 0) = 0`. popup.tsx:350-368 renders exactly those values. Wrong data in one popup card; P2.

findings.title: Service worker deletes the port map entry by tabId on disconnect without checking it is still the current port
findings.impact: `devtoolsPorts.set(tabId, port)` overwrites unconditionally. If a second port for the same tab connects before the first one's disconnect event fires — which happens on panel remount, on DevTools re-dock (undock/dock), and on any React effect re-run — the stale port's disconnect handler deletes the entry belonging to the *new*, live port. The freshly-mounted panel is then permanently orphaned: the worker has an open port it will never post to, and the panel receives nothing while appearing healthy.
findings.fix: Guard the delete: `port.onDisconnect.addListener(() => { if (devtoolsPorts.get(tabId) === port) devtoolsPorts.delete(tabId); });` and disconnect any pre-existing port for the tab before storing the new one.
findings.verifierNote: Code is verbatim: `devtoolsPorts.set(tabId, port)` at line 91 is unconditional and the disconnect closure at 93-95 deletes by tabId with no identity check. The defect is real. But the stated triggers are weaker than claimed: the panel effect deps are `[loadSavedTours]`, a `useCallback(..., [])`, so it does not re-run; there is no StrictMode (app.tsx:1276-1279 renders `<App />` bare); and panel unload/reload is normally sequential (old page torn down, then new page connects). It is a narrow race, not a routine one: P2.

findings.title: accessibility.spec.ts default-imports AxeBuilder from a package that has no such export
findings.evidence: import AxeBuilder from 'axe-playwright';
findings.impact: `axe-playwright` exports named helpers (`injectAxe`, `checkA11y`, `getViolations`, `reportViolations`) — it has no default export and no `AxeBuilder` class. `AxeBuilder` is the API of the different package `@axe-core/playwright`. At runtime `new AxeBuilder({ page })` throws `TypeError: AxeBuilder is not a constructor`, so the two accessibility-scanning tests (lines 9-14 and 16-26) fail before any assertion runs. These are the repo's only automated a11y checks; the README claims accessibility is a first-class feature.
findings.fix: Either swap the dependency to `@axe-core/playwright` in `apps/e2e/package.json` and import `{ AxeBuilder }`, or rewrite the spec against the installed API: `import { injectAxe, getViolations } from 'axe-playwright'` then `await injectAxe(page); const violations = await getViolations(page, '.gf-popover', { runOnly: ['wcag2a','wcag2aa'] })`.
findings.verifierNote: accessibility.spec.ts:2 is verbatim `import AxeBuilder from 'axe-playwright';`. node_modules/axe-playwright@2.2.2 dist/index.d.ts exports only injectAxe, configureAxe, getAxeResults, getViolations, reportViolations, checkA11y, DefaultTerminalReporter — no default export, no AxeBuilder. `new AxeBuilder({page})` throws. Severity lowered to P2: the suite already cannot run at all (see e2e-suite-cannot-run), so this adds no independent shipped impact.

findings.title: `push` and the demo default to api.guideflow.dev, a service with no evidence of existing
findings.evidence: .option('-e, --endpoint <url>', 'API endpoint', 'https://api.guideflow.dev/v1/flows')
findings.impact: README.md:31 lists "push to GuideFlow Cloud" as a shipped CLI capability and README.md:536 documents `guideflow push` as "Publish flows to GuideFlow Cloud". The default endpoint is `api.guideflow.dev`, a domain that appears nowhere else in the repo except as a banner comment (packages/core/tsup.config.ts:17), a devtools popup link (packages/devtools/src/popup/popup.tsx:501) and demo placeholders (apps/demo/src/App.tsx:178, :843). No provisioning, auth-issuance, or account documentation exists anywhere. findings.title: Popover positioning tests cover 4 of 13 placements and never exercise a scrolled viewport
findings.evidence: const viewport = { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 800 }
findings.impact: Every one of the six tests uses `viewport.x === 0 && viewport.y === 0`. But `getViewportRect()` (packages/core/src/engine/popover.ts:154-158) returns `x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY` — page coordinates — while `DefaultRenderer._position` (default-renderer.ts:216) passes a target rect built from `getBoundingClientRect()`, which is viewport-relative. The mixed coordinate systems only diverge once the page is scrolled, and that is precisely the case no test constructs, so `fitsInViewport` silently misjudges every placement on a scrolled page and the popover flips or clamps wrongly. Coverage of the placement matrix is also thin: only `bottom`, `top`, `right` and `center` are asserted — the nine `-start`/`-end` variants and all their fallback sequences (popover.ts:9-23) are untested, as are `scrollTargetIntoView` and `getAbsoluteRect`.
findings.fix: Add a table-driven test over all 13 `PopoverPlacement` values asserting the returned `placement` and geometry, plus explicit cases with `viewport = { x: 0, y: 600, width: 1280, height: 800 }` to pin down the intended coordinate space (and fix whichever of getViewportRect/_position is wrong). Add clamping tests for a target at each viewport edge.
findings.verifierNote: popover.test.ts:7 is verbatim and all six tests use x:0,y:0 viewports; only bottom/top/right/center are asserted, and the twelve FALLBACK_SEQUENCES entries (popover.ts:9-23) plus scrollTargetIntoView and getAbsoluteRect are untouched. The coordinate-mixing bug is real and I reproduced the reasoning: getViewportRect (popover.ts:150-158) returns `x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY` (page coords), default-renderer.ts:216-222 passes `targetRect.left/top` from getBoundingClientRect (viewport coords), fitsInViewport (popover.ts:75-82) then compares `pos.x >= viewport.x` mixing the two, and popover.css:5 is `position: fixed` so the written coords are viewport-relative. Divergence appears only when scrolled — exactly the untested case.

findings.title: No onError hook, no error-reporting integration, and the debug flag only gates a single console.warn
findings.evidence: if (this._options.debug) {
findings.impact: GuideFlowConfig exposes `debug?: boolean`, whose only effect anywhere in core is guarding `console.warn('[GuideFlow]', ...args)` at tour.ts:368-370. There is no `onError` callback, no error-reporting/Sentry integration point, and no docs guidance on capturing failures in production. The `tour:error` event exists but @guideflow/analytics does not subscribe to it (already found), so a library that renders into arbitrary customer DOM, evaluates user-supplied showIf functions, parses untrusted LLM JSON, and touches localStorage/IndexedDB has no supported way to tell its host that anything went wrong. Every failure surfaces as a silent no-op or a console.warn the host never sees.
findings.fix: Add `onError?: (err: GuideFlowError) => void` to GuideFlowConfig, route every current console.warn through it with a structured code (TARGET_NOT_FOUND, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, RENDER_FAILED, AI_PARSE_FAILED), have the analytics collector subscribe to tour:error, and add an 'Error handling in production' docs page.

findings.title: i18n covers only 8 chrome strings — step content itself has no localisation mechanism at all
findings.impact: I18nRegistry translates the 8 fixed UI labels (Next/Back/Skip/etc.), but a Step's title, body, html, media alt text, and action labels are plain strings baked into the FlowDefinition. There is no locale key form, no per-locale flow variant, and no documented pattern beyond 'resolve content yourself with a function'. A team shipping a tour in five languages must build and maintain five FlowDefinitions or hand-roll a resolver in every step's content callback. Combined with the fact that instance.i18n never reaches the renderer, the advertised 'extensible translation registry with locale fallback' delivers essentially nothing for the content users actually read.
findings.fix: Allow StepContent fields to accept a translation key resolved through the instance's I18nRegistry (or accept `Record<locale, StepContent>`), have TourEngine resolve against the active locale, and document the pattern in apps/docs/guide/i18n.md alongside the fixes for the fictional API already found there.

findings.title: No draft/published distinction, no preview or staging mode, and no collaboration or permissions model
findings.impact: A FlowDefinition is either in the shipped bundle or it is not — there is no `status: 'draft' | 'published'`, no preview token, no way to run a tour for internal testers only, and no `gf.preview(flow)` that bypasses persistence gating so an author can re-watch a tour they have already completed (completed/dismissed flags will silently suppress it). Because there is no backend, there is also no notion of who edited a flow, no review step, and no audit trail. Teams evaluating against Chameleon/Appcues, where draft→preview→publish with reviewer approval is table stakes, have no equivalent workflow and no way to safely test a tour in production.
findings.fix: At minimum add `gf.preview(flow)` that starts a flow while bypassing isDismissed/isCompleted/snapshot restore and suppresses analytics, plus a documented convention for gating draft flows behind GuidanceContext.roles. A real draft/publish model requires the backend from no-backend-cms-or-self-hosting-story.

findings.title: Target resolution is a bare document.querySelector — web components and iframes cannot be toured
findings.evidence: return document.querySelector(step.target)
findings.impact: _resolveTarget performs one light-DOM query with no shadowRoot piercing and no same-origin iframe traversal, and there is no way to pass a custom resolver. Any app built on Lit, Stencil, Salesforce LWC, Shoelace, or any design system that encapsulates in shadow DOM cannot target its own components, and any tour step pointing at content inside an embedded iframe silently degrades to the full-screen dark modal. The DevTools selector generator has the same blind spot (already found as selector-no-shadow-dom), so the two halves of the product fail together. This rules out a large class of enterprise apps that competitors handle.
findings.fix: Add a shadow-piercing resolver in packages/core/src/engine/tour.ts that walks open shadowRoots (and optionally same-origin iframes), plus a `resolveTarget?: (selector: string) => Element | null` escape hatch on GuideFlowConfig for closed roots. Mirror the same logic in packages/devtools/src/content/inspector.ts buildSelector.

findings.title: Zero touch/pointer handling and no responsive popover strategy — the library is desktop-keyboard-only
findings.evidence: max-width: calc(100vw - 32px);
findings.impact: A repo-wide grep across packages/core/src for touchstart, touchend, pointerdown, swipe, and matchMedia returns nothing; the only @media rules in the entire stylesheet set are prefers-color-scheme (dark.css:2) and forced-colors (high-contrast.css:2). So on mobile there is no swipe-to-advance, no touch-friendly dismissal, no bottom-sheet fallback for narrow viewports, no viewport-height handling for the mobile URL bar, and no larger touch targets (the hotspot beacon is 12 px). The only concession is a max-width clamp. Navigation on touch devices depends entirely on tapping Next, and the spotlight's fixed-position overlay will fight iOS Safari's dynamic viewport. The Playwright config even declares a Pixel 5 project that has never run.
findings.fix: Add touch handling to TourEngine (swipe left/right to navigate, guarded by a `gestures` config flag), add a narrow-viewport placement strategy in computePosition that falls back to a bottom-sheet layout under ~480 px, size hotspot/hint targets to 44 px minimum, and use dvh units for full-viewport overlays.

findings.title: The only changelog is docs/changelog.html, stuck at v0.1.4 in the unpublished hand-written site, and there is no deprecation policy
findings.impact: There is no root CHANGELOG.md, no per-package CHANGELOG, no GitHub Releases automation, and no release-notes section in the VitePress site. The one changelog that exists lives in docs/ — the orphaned hand-written HTML site that is never built or deployed — and its newest entry is five patch releases behind the published 0.1.9. findings.title: OpenAI and Anthropic clients are constructed without dangerouslyAllowBrowser, so every documented browser integration throws at first call
